You'll run onboarding, enablement, and growth across ElevenLabs' full platform, core speech models, creative tools, and Agents. You'll advise customers on production deployment, not just theory, digging into usage and performance data to catch friction early and keep adoption moving.

You'll also own commercial outcomes for a defined book of business against clear targets: Gross Revenue Retention, Net Revenue Retention, cross-sell, and net expansion. You'll spot expansion opportunities early, own renewals and upsells end to end, and work closely with Sales, Engineering, and CS leadership to turn technical wins into revenue.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of Customer Success, Account Management or Technical Account Management experience supporting complex B2B SaaS, Developer Tools, or AI/ML products in the CEE region

  • Proven experience of owning and managing a defined Book of Business

  • Fluent in English & Polish, preferred

  • Proven experience working across the UK & Ireland market. Knowledge of the landscape and cultural nuances

  • Familiarity and experience with building and deploying AI agents

  • Strong builder mindset - you thrive in ambiguity and being a pioneer, finding ways to innovate across a full region or market to drive revenue outcomes

  • Familiarity and experience with API Integrations, and comfort and knowledge of navigating SDKs

  • Proven experience working cross functionally with Sales, Engineering, Product, and Marketing teams

  • Proven experience driving revenue outcomes, including owning a revenue quota and identifying, qualifying, and closing cross-sell opportunities along with renewals

  • Excellent problem-solving, technical, and analytical skills to address customer needs and concerns

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build and maintain relationships with customers at all levels of an organization

  • Self-motivated and able to work independently in a remote or distributed team environment

This role is remote-first but Warsaw is preferred.

description:
Take your career to new heights with Loopio! ðâ¨

Loopio is a workplace that unleashes learning & growth opportunities for our Loopers. We provide autonomous, challenging work that allows each employee to master their craft. We attract and retain people who are naturally curious, have grit and are eager to grow and build their careers. At Loopio, we genuinely support each other, because true success comes from working as #oneteam.

Loopio is on the hunt for a Senior Software Developer with an AI engineering background who thrives on solving complex problems and is driven by curiosity. If you have taken LLM-based systems from idea to production and want your work to help leading organizations respond to RFPs faster and with more confidence, this is the role for you.

Youâll join a team of Engineers, ML practitioners, Product Managers, and Designers to design and ship AI-powered features, from agentic workflows that reason over long and messy documents to the evaluation and monitoring that keep them reliable in production. At Loopio, we value clean code, evidence-driven decisions, continuous improvement, and knowledge sharing. From shaping technical direction to mentoring teammates, youâll play a key role in scaling our systems and evolving our product.

Weâre deeply collaborative. Whether itâs pair programming, technical design reviews, error-analysis sessions, or whiteboarding ideas, we believe the best solutions are built together. If youâre excited by owning problems from zero, letting evidence drive your decisions, and leaving things better than you found them, letâs build the future together.

Note: This is an existing vacancy on the team

What Youâll Be Doing:

  • Owning problems end to end, from zero. You take an idea or problem through framing, a research plan, build, validation, shipping, and monitoring, and you make fast, honest pursue-or-kill calls along the way.

  • Designing, building, and shipping LLM-based and agentic systems (tool use, multi-step workflows) that plan and execute work over long or messy documents, including layout-aware parsing, extraction, classification, and cross-document reasoning.

  • Partnering closely with the ML team to turn research prototypes into reliable, maintainable features in a shared codebase with a proper test harness and CI workflow, including knowledge-graph-grounded retrieval where it fits.

  • Building evaluation into everything you ship: eval sets and regression suites, at both the task level and the step level, that predict production behavior for single models and multi-step pipelines alike.

  • Digging into the data before modeling, and running systematic error analysis when results fall short. You judge whether a problem demands precision, recall, or coverage, because a missed question costs the customer and a wrong suggestion costs trust.

  • Going below the API when it makes sense: training, fine-tuning, or distilling models, and surveying the research literature to adapt what you find to the problem at hand.

  • Operating AI features live, including tracing, failure triage, and managing cost and latency tradeoffs.

  • Contributing to Loopioâs AI roadmap by evaluating third-party models, establishing patterns for agentic workflows, and defining technical and evaluation guidelines for AI-powered features.

  • Designing and shipping reusable frameworks and shared libraries that raise the bar for how every team at Loopio builds, so good patterns scale instead of being reinvented.

  • Interacting with and gathering detailed feedback from our customers, because you understand that creating a user-centric experience comes first.

  • Explaining tradeoffs, metrics, and failure modes to product and engineering partners in plain language, with write-ups that let others follow your reasoning and act on your results.

  • Mentoring and coaching others, providing technical guidance and helping build an environment of knowledge-sharing and encouraging feedback.

  • Comfortably leading technical design discussions and facilitating technical decision making. Experience as a technical lead is a bonus!

  • Own onboarding and activation for agencies, brokers, and carriers using the Outmarket platform, so customers see value fast and adopt the product widely.

  • Build and maintain trusted relationships with agency principals, department leaders, producers, and account managers.

  • A track record of owning a book of accounts and moving the numbers that matter: adoption, retention, and expansion.

  • Comfort leading onboarding and training for users ranging from agency principals to day-to-day account managers.

  • Strong communication skills. You can run an executive business review in the morning and a hands-on training in the afternoon.

  • The ability to spot patterns across customers and turn them into clear, useful feedback for Product.

  • A builder's mindset. You like creating playbooks, templates, and processes where none exist yet.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and a fast pace. You take ownership without waiting for direction.

Nice to have

  • Experience across multiple lines of business (P&C, Employee Benefits, specialty).

  • Familiarity with agency management systems (e.g. Applied Epic, Vertafore AMS360) or other tools agencies rely on.

  • Experience at an early-stage or high-growth startup.

What you will do

Run our PJM utility programs end to end: registrations, nominations, dispatch, performance calculations and settlements.

Help launch a new program and identify the next ones with Product and Partnerships.

Advise Product and Partnerships on program design, opportunity sizing and utility proposals. You will not draft formal regulatory filings.

Explain program rules in plain language to Sales, customers and Dispatch Ops, and write to utilities and PJM on registration and settlement issues.

Support PJM - ELRP (Load Management) registrations starting in 2028.

Guide and review the work of co-op and junior analysts. This role has no direct reports.

Within 60 days, you know the established program well enough to run it without the team's involvement.

Registrations, nominations, tests, events and quarterly settlements are on time and accurate, and your manager reviews rather than does.

New program registrations are submitted on time with no missed deadlines, and enrolled MW is at or near target.

Baseline and performance methodology is agreed with Engineering and Product before the first dispatch.

A written playbook for the new program exists that someone else could pick up.

Product, Partnerships, Dispatch Ops and utility contacts come to you directly.

Your analysis has informed a program design discussion with Product and Partnerships.

What you bring

Required

3 to 5 years of hands-on energy markets experience in demand response or a closely related area (registrations, performance calculations, settlements), in any ISO or utility program.

Advanced Excel or Google Sheets: trackers, baseline-versus-metered-load calculations, and settlement reconciliations that others can audit.

Basic SQL: read-only queries with joins, aggregations and filters to pull site, interval and dispatch data.

Basic Python, with familiarity with Pandas, to process interval data across many sites and automate repetitive registration and settlement prep.

Clear written communication, including plain-language explanations of program rules and professional correspondence with utilities and ISOs.

Ownership: you make judgment calls on ambiguous program rules, know when to escalate, and build process where none exists.

Availability during core Eastern hours and during test and event windows. PJM, the utilities and all program deadlines run on Eastern time.

Preferred

PJM experience, in this order of relevance: DR programs (ELRP, utility DR programs in PJM states); settlements and performance calculations; capacity market basics (PLCs, nominations, delivery year calendar); wholesale market operations.

title: Senior iOS Engineer, Foundations
description:
We are seeking a Senior iOS Engineer to join Raya Foundations, the platform team that owns the shared foundation every other Raya engineering team builds on. On the client side that means the architecture of our iOS codebase, its modularization and build system, shared libraries and design-system components, CI and release tooling, crash and performance infrastructure, and the AI-collaborative development tooling our iOS engineers use every day.

This is a senior client engineering role with deep technical impact across a large, long-lived swift iOS codebase. The ideal candidate has built and operated high-scale consumer iOS applications end to end, has been the engineer other iOS engineers come to for architecture and tooling, and is excited about modernizing a mature Swift codebase while keeping it shipping every week. Rather than owning one feature surface, you will partner with the product client teams, server engineering, and design to raise the engineering bar across the whole app.

We offer comprehensive medical and dental coverage, $50 a day food delivery budget, equity based employment, a great culture, learning opportunities, unlimited vacation, 12 weeks paid parental leave, and we pay all employees $1,000 a year to go somewhere in the world that they've never been because of our values of human connection, empathy, and curiosity.

Responsibilities

Own the architecture of Raya's iOS codebase: set the patterns and best practices for state management, SwiftUI adoption, navigation, networking, and concurrency, and solve the hard client-side lifecycle problems that span teams.

Drive modernization of a large, long-lived Swift codebase: modularization, SwiftUI alongside UIKit, Swift concurrency, and deliberate management of tech debt. Write the tech specs, make the trade-offs explicit, and sequence the work so it ships incrementally.

Build the shared foundation other iOS engineers build on: design-system components, shared libraries, networking and persistence layers, and the dev harness (build times, CI, test infrastructure, release tooling).

Build and roll out the AI-collaborative development tooling iOS engineers use every day, and set the standards for how we use it on the client.

Improve client production health infrastructure: crash and performance monitoring, alerting, release quality, and the security posture of the app.

Partner with server engineering on API design and client-server state sync, and with the product client teams so new features land on solid patterns.

Requirements

5+ years of professional iOS development experience, with strong proficiency in Swift, UIKit, and MVVM.

Strong experience with RxSwift or similar reactive programming frameworks, and with Redux-style state management patterns.

A track record of shipping consumer mobile apps to large audiences, with strong judgment on architecture, performance, and user experience.

Experience owning client platform or infrastructure work that other engineers depend on (modularizing a large iOS codebase, build and CI systems, shared libraries, design systems, or release tooling) and driving its adoption.

Proven ability to lead projects from concept through launch, balance speed and quality, and own what you ship after it ships.

You use AI coding tools in your daily work, help the team adopt them, and look for opportunities to improve the engineering harness.

What Sets You Apart

Deep experience with SwiftUI alongside UIKit and with Swift concurrency (async/await, actors, strict concurrency), including migrating a mature codebase to them. CoreData a plus!

Experience with Xcode build performance, Swift Package Manager or Bazel/Tuist, and CI/CD for iOS at scale.

Has built developer tooling, agents, or evals that other engineers adopted: code review agents, lint and architecture rules, test generation, or LLM-powered dev harnesses.

Occasional comfort or interest in shipping production backend code (Node.js/TypeScript) alongside the client, and designing the APIs mobile clients depend on.

Experience with mobile security: device trust, certificate pinning, secrets handling, or security remediation on the client.

title: Lifecycle Marketing Manager
description:
Employment type: Full-time
Experience: 4+ years
Reports to: Chris Stella, VP Growth

About Lifeforce

We are in the early stages of a generational shift in how people approach their health. No longer satisfied with the reactive, fragmented care offered by the traditional healthcare system, millions of people are taking a more proactive approach. They want to understand how their bodies work, take control of how they feel and perform, and invest in living longer, healthier lives. Lifeforce is leading this shift as the world's largest longevity medicine program.

Founded alongside clinical and scientific leaders from Cleveland Clinic, Massachusetts General Hospital, and Harvard Medical School, Lifeforce brings together the diagnostics, expertise, and treatments people need to understand and optimize their health, both today and for decades to come. Our comprehensive program combines advanced diagnostics, expert clinicians, dedicated health coaches, and personalized supplement, pharmaceutical, and lifestyle protocols. All delivered from home, at the price of a gym membership.

Overview

Lifeforce is hiring a Lifecycle Marketing Manager to own every message a lead or member gets from us after the first click. You'll run email, SMS, push, and in-app messaging across the full journey: turning leads into members, getting new members through their first diagnostics and clinician visit, keeping members engaged with their protocols, and bringing back the ones who drift.

This is a hands-on role. You will build the journeys, write and test the messages, set up the segments, and read the results yourself. You'll use AI tools to move faster on copy, personalization, and analysis, and you'll build a lifecycle program that scales as our membership, clinician network, and Ultimate Longevity Center (ULC) locations grow.

You'll work closely with growth, product, clinical, coaching, and member experience teams. Paid acquisition brings people to the door. You make sure they walk in, stay, and get results.

Key Responsibilities

Lead Nurture & Conversion

Build and run nurture journeys that turn leads from paid, organic, and referral channels into members. Work with the growth team to match messaging to the ads, landing pages, and offers that brought each lead in. Test offers, timing, and content to raise lead-to-member conversion.

Onboarding & Activation

Own the new-member journey from sign-up through first lab draw, results review, and first clinician and coach visits. Cut drop-off at each step by finding where members get stuck and fixing it with clear, timely messages. Partner with member experience and operations so messages match what members actually see and do.

Retention, Engagement & Win-Back

Build programs that keep members engaged with their protocols, follow-up diagnostics, and coaching. Drive adoption of supplements, prescriptions, and other offerings where they fit a member's plan. Run churn-prevention, win-back, and referral programs.

Segmentation, Testing & Analytics

Build segments and triggers from member behavior, lifecycle stage, and program data. Run a steady testing roadmap across subject lines, content, channels, timing, and offers. Own lifecycle reporting: conversion, activation, retention, churn, and revenue by journey. Use AI tools like Claude to draft and personalize content, analyze results, and speed up production.

Platform & Compliance

Own our lifecycle platform setup, data flows, templates, and deliverability. Work with clinical and compliance teams to keep every message accurate and compliant with HIPAA, TCPA, and CAN-SPAM. Document journeys and processes so the program can scale without adding headcount.

Cross-Functional Partnership

Partner with growth on full-funnel strategy and shared conversion goals. Work with product on in-app messaging, onboarding flows, and member data. Bring member insights back to marketing, product, and clinical teams.

What Success Looks Like

  • In your first 90 days: you've audited our current journeys and data, launched a rebuilt lead nurture and new-member onboarding journey, and set up clear reporting on conversion and activation by stage.
  • In your first year: you're running a full lifecycle program from lead to long-term member, with a steady testing cadence, measurable gains in lead-to-member conversion, activation, and retention, and journeys that scale to new markets and ULC locations.

Qualifications

Required

4+ years of lifecycle, CRM, or retention marketing experience in a consumer subscription, DTC, or membership business. Hands-on experience building journeys in a platform like Braze, Customer.io, Iterable, or Klaviyo. Strong copywriting skills across email, SMS, and push. Comfort with data: segmentation, A/B testing, cohort analysis, and reporting. SQL is a plus. Regular use of AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, or similar) to speed up content and analysis. Clear written and verbal communication. Self-directed and effective in a fully remote environment.

Preferred

Experience in digital health, telehealth, wellness, or healthcare. Working knowledge of HIPAA, TCPA, and CAN-SPAM requirements. Experience with Segment, Amplitude, Mixpanel, or a similar data stack. Experience at a startup or high-growth company. Experience building a lifecycle program from scratch.

Traits for Success

  • Passionate about health, wellness, longevity, or human performance.
  • Writes clearly and cares about the member on the other end of every message.
  • Tests everything and lets the data decide.
  • Comfortable doing the detailed work, not just planning it.
  • Raises problems early and comes with a proposed fix.
  • Comfortable in a fast-moving, high-growth environment.

What We Offer

  • Remote working environment
  • Company-provided computer and other required equipment
  • Generous benefits package including Healthcare, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance
  • Complimentary Lifeforce Membership for Full Time Employees

We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

title: Sr. Manager, Revenue Enablement
description:
Software development is changing fast, and code is no longer written by humans alone. Secure Code Warrior is the AI Software Governance platform that gives organizations visibility into how their software is created, strengthens developer capability, and reduces risk before code reaches production. Built on a decade as the world's leading secure coding training platform, we're trusted by enterprises worldwide. We're a venture-backed company with offices in Australia, the United States, Belgium, Iceland, and the United Kingdom.
Â 
Join Secure Code Warrior and help us in our mission to create a safer digital landscape. Weâre empowering organizations to secure their softwareâno matter how the code is written!

We're looking for a self-starter to own revenue enablement for our global go-to-market team across the US, EMEA and APAC. You'll make sure every seller, BDR, sales engineer and customer success manager can explain what we do, run a sharp discovery conversation with a CISO or VP of Engineering, handle the tough objections, and win against the competition.

This role sits in Product Marketing, so you won't just run programs â you'll build the content yourself: product and competitive enablement, objection handling, onboarding and sales plays. You'll work within a small, fast-moving product marketing team where your work shows up in the field within days, not quarters.

What you'll do

Get the field ready for every launch. Turn new products and capabilities into talk tracks, demo paths, short videos and AI-driven self-training modules, so the field knows the story before customers ask.

Make discovery and objection handling a strength. Build discovery guides for the three people in every deal: the CISO or Head of AppSec, the CTO or VP of Engineering, and the Head of AI Governance. Keep a living objection library grounded in real calls, and run the practice that makes it stick.

Track the competition and find where we win. Follow competitor moves and market trends, mine win/loss data and call recordings, and bring that evidence to Product Marketing to sharpen our messaging. Build battlecards and sales plays backed by proof we can show a customer.

Build learning paths and certifications. Create role-based learning paths and certifications for AEs, SEs and CSMs, so everyone is ready before they pitch something new.

Own onboarding, globally. Run one onboarding program for every new GTM hire, from Sydney to San Francisco to Belgium. Set clear ramp milestones and keep making it faster.

Listen first, then build. Spend time with sellers, BDRs, sales leaders, SEs and customer success to understand what they actually need. Test drafts early, ask for feedback and iterate. Measure what gets used and what helps win deals, and retire what doesn't.

Show up at the big moments. Help shape enablement for Revenue Kickoff and product launches across all three regions.

Who you are

A self-starter. You see what needs doing and do it. You don't need a detailed brief or a big team behind you, and you're happiest building something from a blank page.

A collaborator who asks before building. You'd rather spend an hour with a seller than a week guessing. You ask for feedback early and often, you deliver what the team needs, and you never build in a vacuum and hand it down.

Decisive, with conviction. Listening doesn't mean building by committee. You know which feedback to act on and which to set aside, and you'll move on instinct with limited input rather than wait for consensus. Strong opinions don't knock you off course: you stick with what you know will work, and you say no, kindly and clearly, to what won't.

Crisp and clear. You can turn a complex technical product into something a seller can say in 30 seconds and a CISO will care about. You write tight and cut what doesn't earn its place.

Energized by pace. Our market moves every week. Priorities shift, new competitors appear, AI changes the rules. You find that exciting, not overwhelming, and you know how to ship something good fast and improve it later.

Curious about AI. You don't need to be an expert today, but you're excited to make AI part of how you work. We'll invest in your skills, and you'll help us figure out how AI can make enablement faster and better.

What you bring

6â9 years in revenue or sales enablement, sales engineering, product marketing or another customer-facing role at a B2B software company

3+ years in cybersecurity, application security or DevSecOps, with a real understanding of how CISOs, AppSec leaders and engineering executives evaluate and buy

A portfolio of enablement content you built yourself â talk tracks, demo scripts, battlecards, training â and evidence of what it changed

Experience building onboarding and discovery or objection-handling programs for Enterprise and mid-market sales teams

Comfort with technical topics: the software development lifecycle, code security and AI/LLMs

Experience enabling teams across time zones, with a strong instinct for content people can use on their own

Familiarity with a qualification methodology such as MEDDPICC or Command of the Message, and tools like Salesforce and Clari

Nice to have

Competitive intelligence or product marketing experience

A background as a sales engineer or seller

Experience at a fast-growing company where you were the first or only person in your function

Why you'll like it here

Wide scope, real impact. You'll own enablement end to end and see your work change deals quickly.

A direct line to messaging. What you learn in the field shapes how SCW talks about itself.

Backup when you need it. You'll work alongside a Product Marketing team and SCW's AI Center of Excellence, which will help you build your AI skills and workflows.

A market that matters. AI is changing how software gets built, and security leaders need help keeping up. You'll be helping them do it.

Location

This is a remote role based in the US. We strongly prefer candidates in the Pacific Time zone, so you can work with teams in EMEA in the morning and APAC in the afternoon. Some travel for Revenue Kickoff and regional events.

You're joining us at an exciting stage of our journey, and youâre a key piece to what comes next. Expect real room to create impact and deliver on your ideas. The pace is quick and the bar is high; in return, you get genuine ownership and the kind of growth that only comes from building something that matters.

We also know you do your best work when you're rested and energized. Flexibility here runs on trust: we trust you to deliver when it counts, and we trust you to take the time you need to recharge. With teammates around the world, your hours can flex to fit your life, backed by generous leave and work-from-home options that help you make work work for you.

You'll join a tight-knit team that values humility and giving back, both to the community and to each other. Making the world a little brighter as we make it more secure is part of being a Warrior.

We live and work by the Warrior Code. It means getting feedback you can trust, shared without fear. It means no genius jerks: how you treat people counts as much as what you deliver. We do what we say we'll do, we celebrate the wins properly, and we do the right thing even when no one's watching. Come as you are, bring your best, and we'll do the same.

title: Founders Associate (m/w/d) - AI Roll-up
description:
We are building Germany's leading AI-powered tax advisory group. Many business owners want a tax advisor who acts as a true sparring partner: proactive, responsive and strategic. What they often get is a service provider that books receipts and files returns, with little real advice. We're building the alternative.

Taxforce is part of a new category: the AI-powered roll-up. We acquire established tax advisory firms, bring them onto our AI-native platform and grow them, both organically and through further acquisitions. Founded in 2025, we're starting with healthcare professionals, a complex and underserved segment.

This is a €40B market in Germany alone, with processes that have barely changed in decades and a generation of firm owners looking for a successor. AI now enables a fundamental shift, and there are no playbooks yet. We're writing them. We're a small, highly ambitious team in Berlin, backed by €5M from Tenet VC and founded by alumni of Goldman Sachs, Harvard Business School, Y Combinator and the former Klarna Head of Engineering.


The role

We are transforming the tax advisory market with a dual strategy. We build verticalized services, starting with healthcare professionals. At the same time, we take over established firms whose owners are looking for a successor, a need that keeps growing as the market ages, and integrate them as we go. You work directly with our founders on making both work together: acquiring firms, integrating them and making them run on our platform. You own each workstream from the first question to a result you can see in the numbers, and you take on more of the group as it grows.

Tasks

  • M&A: Lead acquisitions, from market research and screening to firm analysis, business cases and due diligence.

  • Integration: Lead the workstreams that bring acquired firms into the group, from the first day after closing to stable operations.

  • Operations design: Build the playbooks, processes and KPIs we use to run a growing group of tax firms, and make sure they work on the ground.

  • AI and product rollout: Work with our engineering team to roll out our platform in our firms, automate manual workflows and track adoption and impact.

  • Founder-led projects: Own topics that cut across teams or have no owner yet, such as board and investor materials or financing processes, and drive them to an outcome.


Requirements

  • 2 to 3 years of experience: In strategy consulting, investment banking, private equity, transaction services or an operating role at a high-growth startup.

  • Financial fluency: You understand P&Ls, balance sheets and cash flows and build models that others can read and check.

  • Execution, not just analysis: You take your recommendation through implementation, including on the ground with the teams in our firms.

  • Clear judgement: You break down unstructured problems, separate facts from assumptions and decide even when the data stays incomplete.

  • AI-native: You use AI tools every day and build automations yourself.

  • German language skills: Our clients and the firms we acquire speak German, so we require fluent German (C2) and strong English.

  • A plus, not a must: Experience in tax, accounting or another regulated market.

Benefits

  • Work directly with experienced founders: Learn first-hand from a team with backgrounds at Goldman Sachs, Harvard Business School, Bain & Company and Klarna, and from a former Y Combinator founder.

  • Build a new category: Shape how an AI-powered roll-up is built in one of Germany's largest professional services markets.

  • Ownership from day one: Own workstreams on live deals, firms and clients, with results you can measure.

  • Front-row seat to AI in the real world: See how AI transforms a traditional industry and help build it.

  • Room to grow: Take on more responsibility and your own area as the group grows.

  • Competitive salary: Pay that reflects your experience and the impact of your role.

The details

Full-time, permanent position, start as soon as possible, on-site in our Berlin office five days a week.

How to apply

Send us your CV. Our process has four steps: a first call, a culture interview, a quantitative case study based on a real case from our work, and a final round with the founders. It is thorough, and we move quickly.

title: Senior/Staff Platform Engineer (m/f/x)
description:
Your Role

We ship fast, and we intend to keep shipping fast. The consequence is that our system is outgrowing the amount of deliberate design that went into it. We run AI agents over customer documents in a domain where being wrong is expensive, and a lot of the load-bearing decisions about how those fit together are still implicit.

You will be making those decisions explicit and then making them hold. That means codifying golden paths, building the shared primitives and APIs that product engineers work on top of, owning the architecture of the system as a whole, and establishing what our reliability actually needs to be before an incident establishes it for us.

Platform at Cortea sits between software engineering, DevOps and SRE. Its customers are other engineers. This is not a DevOps role under a different name: you will spend more time in application code than in YAML, and the reason we want infrastructure experience is that we don't believe you can design a system well without being able to run it.

The bar we are hiring against is someone who has taken a system from nothing to production and owned it end to end. You picked the technology, argued the tradeoffs in writing, provisioned the infrastructure, and were responsible for it when it broke.


On AI

We use AI heavily and we want you to. What we are not looking for is someone who outsources their judgment to it.

The mental model of this system has to live in your head, not in a context window. Use agents to move quickly on implementation. Do the design, the reasoning and the writing yourself, and be able to defend every decision you ship.


What you'll do

Four areas, roughly in the order you will spend time on them. You won't work on all of them at once, but you should be open to any of them.

Product platform. Make the easiest way for product engineers to do something (the paved road, or golden path) also the most secure, reliable and scalable way by default. Build the shared primitives, libraries and APIs that hide complexity and carry our quality and observability standards with them. Own the architecture and the core stack: what gets standardized, what gets reused, and where the system should be in eighteen months.

Infrastructure, observability and reliability. Infrastructure as code by default, from cloud resources through to dashboards and alerts. Provision, run and tune our Kubernetes cluster and cloud footprint, and keep CI fast as the deploy rate grows. Define SLIs for the workloads that
matter, build SLOs on top of them, and make the alerting high-signal enough that people trust it. Drive down AI and infrastructure spend.

Security and compliance. Keep the internal foundations secure by default: IAM, dependency management, secrets. Own the authentication and authorization stack, including ReBAC models covering both humans and agents. Implement SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls without taxing every future change.

AI dev tooling. Keep product engineers and their agents on the paved road by making sure the documentation and agent guidelines they need are in place. Shorten the path from design to implementation with standardized automations and development environments that stay close to production.


What this looks like in practice

  • A system of record for managing and distributing constantly evolving agent configurations, under strict auditability and tenant isolation requirements

  • The harnesses powering our AI agents, abstracting over use cases that change faster than the code

  • Centralized progress tracking that holds up across a growing number of parallel agent executions

  • Usage-based tenant billing with quotas and rate limiting across a growing set of products

  • SLIs for the background job system behind our agents (execution latency, AI spend, memory, CPU), then fixing the bottlenecks they expose at both the application and infrastructure level

  • A document pipeline handling dozens of file formats, very large spreadsheets and hundreds of parallel uploads, under a strong reliability requirement


You will fit into this role if you…

  • Have designed, built and operated distributed systems end to end, and enjoy understanding how every part interacts with the rest

  • Are strong at backend software engineering and at DevOps/SRE, and don't think of those as separate jobs

  • Write design docs, RFCs, ADRs, postmortems

  • Reach for simple, boring solutions first, can tell essential complexity from accidental, and know which corners are safe to cut and which ones compound

  • Can turn a hard problem on its head and find the alternative nobody proposed

Concretely, you have scaled Postgres or another relational transactional database under real load, run production Kubernetes, and built observability rather than inherited it: SLIs, SLOs, distributed tracing.

No one checks every box. If you have designed a system from scratch, run it in production, and can explain in writing why it is shaped the way it is, let's talk.


Nice-to-haves that are a plus:

  • Durable workflow orchestrators like Temporal, and background job and queue processing generally

  • Infrastructure for LLM-based products or agentic systems

  • Audit, finance, compliance, or another high-accuracy domain

  • Azure and/or GCP


This is probably not the right role if…

  • You would describe application code as someone else's responsibility. A large share of platform work here happens inside the product codebase.

  • Your answer to reliability is more process. We want guardrails, not gates.

  • You need a well-defined system to work in. Ours is not one yet, and shaping it is the job.


What you will get

  • You own the brand and shape how the product feels. Work face-to-face with experienced founders and learn directly from customer insights.

  • Real influence on strategy. In a small team of excellent engineers and operators with high autonomy, you will shape product direction. Best idea wins, regardless of seniority.

  • Fast, ambitious, and fun team. Decisions get made in hours, not weeks. Rapid experimentation is the default.

  • Meaningful equity and competitive salary. You are one of the first to build this, and you share in the upside.

  • A mission that matters. Building intelligent systems for a $200bn industry. From Berlin, with AI at the core.


Interview process

  • First Call — Intro to Cortea with Liza

  • Second Call — Technical interview with Dan

  • Third Call — Deep dive into our culture with our Co-Founder Philipp

  • On-site Day (Berlin) — Meet the team and work on a real problem together

title: Senior/Staff AI Engineer, Quality & Evals (m/f/x)
description:
About us

We’re Cortea, a Berlin startup transforming audits with AI. Manual, document-heavy audits waste expert time while demand keeps rising. Our AI-powered software and specialized AI agents remove the repetitive work so auditors can focus on judgment.

Backed by top-tier VCs with >15m EUR funding, with a working product and paying customers, we’re rapidly scaling.

We value first-principles thinking, speed, trust, and kindness. We build side by side in our Berlin office.

Your Role

We are looking for an engineer with strong backend, data, and AI systems experience to build the evaluation and observability foundation for production-grade LLM agents used in complex audit workflows.

This role sits at the intersection of backend engineering, data infrastructure, and AI quality. You will build the evaluation systems that power our multimodal retrieval agents and continuously improve critical quality metrics across current and future pipelines.

You’ll work at the edge of applied AI and information retrieval, building multimodal agentic pipelines and solving hard context and agent-harness engineering problems.

This is not a traditional analytics, BI, or dashboarding role. You should expect to write production code, design data architecture, work inside backend systems, and directly improve the quality, cost, reliability, and performance of LLM-based agents.

What you’ll do

You will help build and operate the technical systems around our AI agents, with a focus on data infrastructure, evaluation, observability, and optimization. You will:

  • Build online and offline evaluation systems for LLM agents, including pipelines that use golden datasets, ground-truth data, human review workflows, and experiment results.

  • Create automated quality gates so changes to prompts, context, models, or agent logic can be tested before reaching production.

  • Analyze large volumes of agent traces and executions in columnar and analytical databases such as BigQuery or ClickHouse to identify failure modes, quality regressions, latency issues, reliability gaps, and cost optimization opportunities.

  • Build reliable data retention and replay mechanisms for long-term analysis of production agent behavior.

  • Manage observability tools for tracing, monitoring, debugging, and experiment management of our audit agents.

  • Team up with backend engineers to improve the speed and reliability of our retrieval and reasoning agents.

You will fit into the role if you...

  • Have strong Python and/or backend engineering experience.

  • Have a solid understanding of how LLM and agent systems are evaluated—including deterministic checks, ground truth, LLM-as-judge, human review, and quality metrics—and can reason about when each approach is appropriate.

  • Have deployed and operated systems in the cloud, ideally on GCP.

  • Have hands-on experience building end-to-end retrieval or ML pipeline evaluation systems and using LLM observability or experimentation tools such as Braintrust, MLflow, Langfuse, or Weights & Biases.

  • Are comfortable working with analytical databases, data warehouses, columnar stores, and high-volume event or trace data.

  • Understand system design, reliability, observability, monitoring, logging, debugging, and operational trade-offs.

  • Bring senior-level engineering judgment: you can make architectural decisions, communicate trade-offs, and build systems that other engineers can extend.

  • Are comfortable with ambiguity, able to reason from first principles, and excited to build infrastructure for AI systems that are actively used in production.

Nice-to-haves that are a plus:

  • Designing data pipelines, ETL/ELT workflows, event-processing systems, or feedback loops for production data.

  • Building infrastructure around LLM-based products or agentic systems, including optimizing LLM usage, context windows, reasoning tokens, or model selection.

  • Working with production traces from complex distributed systems.

  • Building internal platforms for engineers, domain experts, or operations teams.

  • Using workflow orchestration systems such as Temporal or similar.

  • Familiarity with audit, finance, compliance, or other high-accuracy domains.

  • Experience in an early-stage startup or fast-moving engineering environment.

No-one checks every box. If you’ve shipped retrieval systems and like owning evaluations and pipelines, let’s talk.

title: Head of Operational Integration
description:
About Andercore

Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials and goods for energy and infrastructure. We execute trade and distribution end-to-end, on our own account, at the speed of compute - and we are becoming the supplier of record for the entire industry.

Industrial procurement is a €900B market in Europe alone and the largest manual market on earth. 95% of customers have no direct access to global supply chains. Materials pass through four or five intermediaries before they reach a site, and 40% of the margin evaporates on the way. For decades, the operating system of this industry was people: people to source, negotiate, finance, ship, and sell.

We built the alternative from scratch. We are the supplier. We buy from global sources and sell to European customers on our own account. Our AI runs the full trade: sourcing, quality, pricing, sales, logistics, credit, and financing. One request. A firm quote in minutes. Delivered on time. For the customer, it feels like buying from their preferred local supplier. No warehouses. No fleet. No inventory risk. Every trade is pre-sold before it is bought.

We are also the credit counterparty. Customers are scored and insured in minutes and get up to 60 days of payment terms priced into the quote itself. The working capital behind every trade is bank-funded, not equity-funded.

Where we are today:

  • Strong triple-digit-million euro turnover run rate, the majority of it from repeat customers

  • Seven European markets live, sourced from suppliers across Asia and beyond

  • 80+ people across Berlin (HQ), London, and Shanghai

  • $90M raised in equity and debt, including our $40M Series B, from Atomico, Project A, Target Global, and Inven Capital - with working capital facilities from UniCredit and KfW

The margin is in the bits. The moat is in the atoms. We are building the supplier of record for industrial materials - and redefining how global trade works in one of the largest and most essential industries on earth.

Acquisitions are our second growth path. We buy established industrial distribution businesses in the EUR 20-40M revenue range, owners and management stay on board, and we connect them to our platform, our procurement, our financing lines and our AI stack. Three deals are live, two are close to signature, and at run rate we intend to close around five per year out of a mapped universe of roughly 200 targets.

Role Overview

You own what happens after signing.

Origination, valuation and deal execution sit with the CEO and our senior M&A advisor. Your mandate starts the day a company becomes part of Andercore and it ends when that company runs better than it did before.

These are analog businesses. Fifteen years old, owner-led, hemdsärmelig, a well-run P&L and almost no technology underneath it. They are profitable, they are growing, and they are at their operational limit. Our hypothesis is that our platform, our purchasing power, our credit facilities and our automation take them past that limit. Your job is to find out on the ground whether that hypothesis holds, in which order, and at what pace - and then to make it happen with the management team, not to them.

We do not arrive as the saviour with the AI magic box. We say so explicitly to every seller, and you will hold that line.

What You Will Own

Holding Management from Day 1

  • Access to accounting and financials from day one, monthly numbers on a fixed close, one reporting framework across all acquired entities.

  • Set the baseline: revenue, margin, working capital, cash, customer and supplier concentration. No opinion without the number behind it.

  • Pick up the commitments made during due diligence and turn them into the operating rhythm of the first 100 days.

  • Run the portfolio as a financial participation first. Both companies are growing. Do not put anything into a skid.

On-the-Ground Diagnosis

  • Spend real time inside the acquired businesses and find out where they actually stand, which is never where they say they stand.

  • Map the connection points: procurement, pricing, inventory, sales productivity, logistics, financing, ERP, reporting.

  • Test our integration theses against reality, quantify the ones that hold, kill the ones that do not, and bring the correction back to the CEO fast.

Value Creation

  • Sequence and land the levers with the management team: central procurement, our credit and working-capital facilities, pricing, sales productivity, customer intelligence, automation of manual back office.

  • Decide with the CEO what gets centralized, what stays entrepreneurial, and what we take from them - the flow runs in both directions, several of these companies do things better than we do.

  • Track every lever against the original investment case in euros.

Owner and Management Relationship

  • Be the peer of a Geschäftsführer who built a EUR 30M business himself. Credibility comes from having done operating work, not from a framework.

  • Be the one who checks whether things are as good as they are described, and who says it out loud when they are not. The CEO stays the partner; you bring the uncomfortable version.

  • Manage expectations in the other direction too: we are not a service provider that solves the acquired company's problems for it.

Playbook and Team

  • Codify integration into a repeatable capability: Day-1 checklist, reporting standard, diagnostic framework, lever library, 100-day plan.

  • Make the fourth acquisition faster than the first, then build and lead the team that runs them in parallel.

Scope Boundaries / What This Role Is Not

  • Not M&A. No origination, no valuation, no LOI, no SPA. That sits with the CEO and our senior M&A advisor.

  • Not a PMO. Nobody here sends a 400-line integration plan with traffic lights to an owner-manager. That gets you thrown out of the room, correctly.

  • Not a consulting engagement. You are measured on the numbers of the acquired companies, not on the quality of the analysis.

  • Not a corporate integration role. These are not hierarchical organizations that execute what the centre decides.

  • Not a process you inherit. There is none yet. You build it.

What We Are Looking For

You are an operator out of a private equity value-creation or portfolio operations team, or a generalist from strategy and transformation with real time spent inside operating companies. Roughly eight to twelve years in.

You bring:

  • At least one integration or post-close situation you personally carried, where you can name the specific knotty problem you solved and why it worked. We will ask for that story in the first interview.

  • Operating substance: you have sat in procurement, pricing, supply chain, finance or sales of a real company, not only next to it.

  • Geländegängigkeit. You are comfortable with an entrepreneur who is highly intelligent, rough around the edges, and holds two cars and a boat inside the company. Nothing about that scenario throws you.

  • People work as roughly half the job. Influence without formal authority, because these managing directors did not sign up to be managed.

  • A strong observer. You read a business and a person quickly and accurately.

  • Fluent German and English. German is not optional; these conversations happen in German.

  • Fluency with modern AI tooling and the instinct to automate your own work. You do not need to be an engineer.

You do not need five PMI programmes on your CV. We would rather you had none than that you learned to fill in lists instead of thinking.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first 12 months:

  • Every acquired entity reports monthly on one framework, on a fixed close, with us having access to accounting.

  • Each acquisition has its integration thesis validated or killed with numbers within 90 days of closing.

  • The acquired businesses keep growing. No customer, supplier or key person lost to the transaction.

  • The first value-creation levers are live and their P&L impact is measurable in euros.

  • A documented playbook exists, and the next integration starts faster than the last.

Over time you own integration and value creation for the whole group at a pace of several acquisitions per year, and build the team that delivers it.

Package

  • Fixed base plus a variable component tied directly to the success of each integration.

  • Virtual equity in Andercore at the current strike, with meaningful upside if we build what we intend to build.

  • Direct work with the Founder & CEO, the M&A advisor, the Board and our investors.

title: Head of Sales - Italy
description:
About Andercore

Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials and goods for energy and infrastructure. We execute trade and distribution end-to-end, on our own account, at the speed of compute - and we are becoming the supplier of record for the entire industry.

Industrial procurement is a €900B market in Europe alone and the largest manual market on earth. 95% of customers have no direct access to global supply chains. Materials pass through four or five intermediaries before they reach a site, and 40% of the margin evaporates on the way. For decades, the operating system of this industry was people: people to source, negotiate, finance, ship, and sell.

We built the alternative from scratch. We are the supplier. We buy from global sources and sell to European customers on our own account. description:

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

We are a special projects team within Proxima’s engineering organisation, using software and computation to fundamentally change how complex machines are designed and built. We take on problems where a small team can deliver a step change in capability, with the goal of getting a stellarator connected to the grid as fast as possible.

As a Computational Engineer, you will bring together mechanical engineering experience and strong software development skills. You will work at the intersection of AI and computational engineering, developing approaches to problems that established tools cannot currently solve.

You will build things yourself: formulate problems, develop algorithms, write software, and test it against real engineering needs. Your experience with hardware will help you see what really moves the needle.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Make engineering tools work together. Connect CAD, PDM, and PLM systems with computational workflows so engineers and agents can use information across tool boundaries.

  • Stay at the frontier and help to move it. Follow advances in AI and computational engineering, test promising ideas quickly, and develop new approaches where existing methods fall short.

  • Ship early and iterate fast. Work side by side with fast-paced engineering teams, put working tools into their hands early, and improve them through short feedback cycles on real projects.

WHO YOU ARE

  • Strong Python development skills, demonstrated through substantial engineering tools or computational models.

  • Experience taking mechanical hardware into manufacture, assembly, or test.

  • Depth in mechanical design, analysis, manufacturing, or integration.

  • The ability to reason from first principles and tackle problems without established solutions.

  • Care for software quality, usability, and adoption.

  • Ambition, initiative, and a focus on getting hardware delivered.

  • Understanding of finite element methods, including modelling assumptions, boundary conditions, mesh convergence, and validation.

  • Experience with some of the following: CAD-as-code, PDM/PLM systems, HPC or cloud computing, and AI agents.

title: Scientist, Model Validation and Experimental Data Analysis
description:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.


TEAM AND ROLE

  • Shape the architecture of the world’s first commercial fusion power plant – Own system-level decisions that determine how a first-of-a-kind energy technology is designed, integrated, and ultimately deployed at scale.

  • Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges in industry – Work across tightly coupled disciplines (plasma physics, magnets, cryogenics, manufacturing, controls, and more) to resolve critical trade-offs and turn cutting-edge science into a functioning product.

  • Build real hardware with a pragmatic, fast-moving team from all over the world – Combine advanced simulation and systems thinking with a strong execution mindset, focusing on practical engineering solutions that accelerate the path to commercial fusion energy.

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

  • You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world.

  • You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals.

  • Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey.

  • Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent.

YOUR IMPACT

You will make Proxima's plasma simulation stack trustworthy by confronting it with reality. Every prediction we make for Alpha – Proxima's Q>1 experimental stellarator – and for Stellaris, our commercial power plant, rests on models whose credibility has to be earned against real measurements from an operating device.

W7-X is where we earn it. You will take our integrated modeling framework, FUS3, and our Bayesian plasma state estimation workflow to W7-X data: reconstruct the plasma state from diagnostic measurements, compare our predictive models against what the machine actually did, and turn the discrepancies into a prioritized map of where our physics is right, where it is not, and what we must fix before Alpha's first plasma. Modeling sits on Alpha's operational critical path and cannot be backfilled after first plasma – this role is how we get ahead of it.

You will be the person in the group who lives at the intersection of modeling and experiment: fluent enough in the physics to know what a model should predict, and close enough to the diagnostics to know what the data can actually support.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Validate Proxima's predictive plasma models against W7-X experimental data – neoclassical and turbulent transport, 3D equilibrium, ECRH deposition, pellet fueling and drift, bootstrap current and iota evolution – and record each comparison as a reproducible validation report with quantitative agreement metrics, stated limitations, and a pinned regression test

  • Reconstruct the plasma state from real diagnostic measurements using our time-dependent Bayesian state-estimation workflow (Thomson scattering, interferometry, CXRS, ECE, XICS, bolometry, magnetics), with calibrated uncertainties, and benchmark it against established analyses such as Minerva/IDA reconstructions and ASTRA power-balance results

  • Work with raw and pre-processed diagnostic data, not just analyzed profiles – instrument geometry, sightlines, calibrations and the caveats that come with them – and own the forward models, noise models and profile fits that feed transport analysis

  • Validate against databases of discharges rather than single shots, across W7-X magnetic configurations and operating regimes, so the output is a map of model applicability and parameter trends rather than one-off discrepancy reports

  • Act as a technical interface to W7-X and IPP: scope and prioritize data requests, spend time on site in Greifswald working alongside diagnosticians and operators, and propose and support experiments that directly target our model gaps

  • Feed validation back into design – convert diagnostic placement and observability studies on W7-X into requirements for Alpha's diagnostic set, and into realistic uncertainty models for the synthetic measurements we use to design against

  • Extend the modeling stack itself: mappers from experimental archives into IMAS, synthetic diagnostics, and analysis workflows, so that interpreting a shot end-to-end – raw data to reconstructed plasma state to physics quantities – runs in minutes and is reproducible by anyone in the group

  • As Alpha approaches operation, help stand up the between-shot analysis loop that will run on day one

WHO YOU ARE

  • PhD in plasma physics, fusion science, or a closely related discipline

  • Hands-on experience with experimental data from a magnetic confinement device – you have dealt with diagnostics, calibrations, systematic errors, and all the ways real data is messier than simulation output

  • Experience reconstructing the plasma state from measurements: profile fitting, integrated data analysis, equilibrium reconstruction, or power and particle balance analysis

  • Strong grounding in transport, equilibrium, and heating physics – enough to tell a code bug from a physics discovery

  • Rigorous about uncertainty; you treat a validation claim without error bars on both sides as incomplete

  • Comfortable writing and maintaining scientific software – version control, testing, and reproducibility are habits, not overhead

  • Can communicate effectively with physicists, diagnosticians, engineers, and experimentalists, and work productively inside an external collaboration

  • Self-directed; able to identify what needs to be done and execute

  • Willing to travel regularly to Greifswald, and later to the Alpha site

NICE TO HAVE

  • W7-X experience - operations, diagnostics, or data analysis, and familiarity with the W7-X data archive and Minerva

  • Stellarator physics background

  • Bayesian inference, uncertainty quantification, or machine learning applied to experimental data

  • Experience with integrated modeling and transport codes (FUSE, OMFIT, ASTRA, TRANSP, FUSE, JINTRAC, or similar) and with neoclassical (SFINCS, DKES, NEO) or gyrokinetic (GENE, CGYRO, GX, or similar) codes

  • Julia and Python programming – our integrated modeling framework is written in Julia

  • Familiarity with the IMAS data model

  • Familiarity with AI-assisted development tools

  • A track record of published validation studies or successful experimental proposals

Als Growth Marketing Manager verantwortest du den Funnel vom ersten Kontakt bis zum registrierten, aktivierten Kunden. Du berichtest direkt an die Gründer und bist unsere erste dedizierte Marketing-Person. Du fängst nicht bei null an: Paid, SEO/GEO, LinkedIn-Content und Outbound laufen bereits als agentengesteuerte Systeme („Maschinen“) aus Git-Repos heraus. Deine Aufgabe ist es, sie zu betreiben, zu schärfen und daraus eine planbare Pipeline zu machen.

ICP - Aktuell liegt der Fokus auf operativ tätigen Tech-/SaaS-GmbHs und Dienstleistungsunternehmen (Professional Services) mit etwa 250.000–2 Mio. € Umsatz; Holdings und Neugründungen kommen über den Self-Service.

Deine Aufgaben:

Du verantwortest folgende Bereiche. Die meisten existieren bereits in irgendeiner Form – es geht also darum, sie zu betreiben, zu messen und zu skalieren, nicht darum, sie von 0 aufzubauen.

  • Demand-Gen-Strategie und Planung

  • SEO und GEO

    • Du baust Autorität auf: Backlinks, Tool-Verzeichnisse, Erwähnungen in Open-Source-Projekten und bei Partnern.

  • Organic Social und Gründer-Marken
    • Du betreibst das LinkedIn-Content-System für die Unternehmensseite und die Profile der Gründer – jeweils mit eigener Tonalität.

  • Outbound via Linkedin
    • Du betreibst LinkedIn-Outbound (Sales Navigator und Dripify) auf Basis signalbasierter Listen, z. B. Unternehmen, die gerade eine Teilzeit-Buchhaltungskraft suchen.
    • Du testest und skalierst Sequenzen mit von Agenten geschriebenen, individuellen Nachrichten pro Lead und übergibst qualifizierte Antworten an den Vertrieb.

  • Produktmarketing und Launches
    • Du verantwortest die Positionierung und das Messaging-Framework („Das autonome Back-Office“) über Website, Anzeigen und Vertriebsmaterial hinweg.
    • Du bringst jeden Feature-Launch durch unseren Launch-Workflow: Demo-Video, Blogartikel (DE/EN), LinkedIn-Posts, Kunden-E-Mail, Vertriebsvorlagen, Changelog.
    • Du leitest die großen saisonalen Kampagnen, beginnend mit der Jahresabschluss-Saison – inklusive Reichweite über Influencer, Podcasts und Partner.

  • Website und Conversion
    • Du verantwortest die Marketing-Website (Astro, Tailwind, Git-basiert) und veröffentlichst Seiten selbst mithilfe von KI-Tools.
    • Du baust und testest Landingpages pro ICP, Lösung und Kampagne und verbesserst den Weg vom Besuch zur Registrierung und Demo-Buchung.

  • Marketing Ops, Tracking und Brevo CRM
    • Du verantwortest das Conversion-Tracking durchgängig: GA4, Google Tag Manager, Google-Ads-Conversions und Offline-Conversions aus dem CRM.
    • Du hältst das Brevo-CRM sauber: Lifecycle-Phasen, Deal-Pipeline, Automatisierungen in n8n, Make und Zapier.
    • Du stellst sicher, dass jeder Euro Paid-Budget bis zu Registrierungen, Opportunities und Umsatz nachverfolgt werden kann.

  • Lifecycle, Aktivierung und Bewertungen
    • Du verantwortest Onboarding- und Aktivierungs-E-Mails, die Testnutzer dazu bringen, ihre Bank zu verbinden und ihre ersten Belege hochzuladen.
    • Du betreust Kunden-Newsletter und Bewertungskampagnen (Trustpilot) und unterstützt das Co-Marketing mit unseren Vertriebspartnern.

Das bringst du mit:

  • Berufserfahrung im Online-Marketing, idealerweise im SaaS- oder B2B-Umfend

  • Fundierter Umgang mit KI-Tools zur Automatisierung von Marketingprozessen und Content-Erstellung - GitHub Repository (Must Have)

title: Senior Fundraiser*in – Stiftungen & Unternehmensförderung
description:
Du gewinnst Förderpartner. Wir bringen Finanzbildung an Deutschlands Schulen.

Du bist erfahren im Fundraising und weißt, wie man Stiftungen und Unternehmen als Förderpartner gewinnt? Du hast bereits erfolgreich Fördermittel für eine gemeinnützige Organisation eingeworben und möchtest deine Erfahrung nutzen, um noch mehr gesellschaftliche Wirkung zu erzielen?

Dann suchen wir genau dich!

Mit unserem Bildungsprojekt Zukunftstag – Dein Crashkurs fürs Leben vermitteln wir jungen Menschen an Schulen wichtige Alltagskompetenzen rund um Finanzen, Steuern, Wohnen und Versicherungen.

Damit wir noch mehr Jugendliche erreichen können, suchen wir eine erfahrene Fundraising-Persönlichkeit, die eigenständig neue Förderpartner gewinnt und unser Fördernetzwerk deutschlandweit ausbaut.

Wichtig: Wir suchen ausdrücklich jemanden mit praktischer Erfahrung in der aktiven Fördermittelakquise. Du solltest bereits erfolgreich Stiftungen oder Unternehmen als Förderpartner für eine gemeinnützige Organisation gewonnen haben.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Aktive Fördermittelakquise: Du identifizierst und kontaktierst gezielt Stiftungen, Unternehmen und weitere potenzielle Förderpartner, insbesondere auf regionaler und lokaler Ebene.

  • Gewinnung neuer Förderpartner: Du überzeugst potenzielle Förderer von unserer Bildungsmission und gewinnst sie für die Finanzierung konkreter Zukunftstage.

  • Eigenverantwortliches Fundraising: Du begleitest den gesamten Akquiseprozess von der Recherche und Erstansprache über persönliche Gespräche bis zur erfolgreichen Förderzusage.

  • Aufbau langfristiger Förderbeziehungen: Du entwickelst bestehende Förderpartnerschaften weiter und gewinnst Förderer für eine dauerhafte Zusammenarbeit.

  • Entwicklung überzeugender Förderangebote: Du erstellst individuelle Förderanfragen, Kooperationskonzepte und Förderanträge.

  • Systematischer Ausbau unseres Fördernetzwerks: Du entwickelst eine kontinuierliche Akquise-Pipeline und arbeitest zielgerichtet daran, unser Fördervolumen nachhaltig zu steigern.

Das bringst du mit

Diese Voraussetzungen sind uns besonders wichtig:

  • Mehrjährige praktische Berufserfahrung im Fundraising einer NGO, Stiftung oder anderen gemeinnützigen Organisation.

  • Nachweisbare Erfolge in der aktiven Gewinnung von Fördermitteln, insbesondere durch die Ansprache von Stiftungen und Unternehmen.

  • Erfahrung in der eigenständigen Identifikation, Ansprache und Gewinnung neuer Förderpartner.

  • Sehr gute Kommunikationsfähigkeiten und ein überzeugendes, professionelles Auftreten gegenüber potenziellen Förderern.

  • Freude an der aktiven Akquise und die Bereitschaft, regelmäßig auf neue potenzielle Förderpartner zuzugehen.

  • Eine selbstständige, strukturierte und ergebnisorientierte Arbeitsweise.

  • Identifikation mit unserer Mission und unseren Werten: Entschlossenheit, Respekt, Verantwortung und Kooperation.

Du passt besonders gut zu uns, wenn du nicht nur Förderanträge verwaltet, sondern selbst aktiv neue Förderpartner gewonnen hast.

Das bieten wir dir

  • Echte gesellschaftliche Wirkung: Deine Fundraising-Erfolge ermöglichen unmittelbar neue Zukunftstage und damit Finanzbildung für Tausende Jugendliche.

  • Attraktive Vergütung: Je nach Erfahrung und Erfolg sind 45.000 bis 100.000 € Jahresgehalt möglich.

  • Eigenverantwortung: Du übernimmst eine zentrale Rolle beim Ausbau unseres Fundraisings und gestaltest unsere weitere Entwicklung aktiv mit.

  • Flexibles Arbeiten: Modernes Büro in Frankfurt am Main und Homeoffice-Möglichkeiten.

  • Dynamisches Team: Motivierte Kolleginnen und Kollegen, kurze Entscheidungswege und flache Hierarchien.

  • Überzeugendes Förderprodukt: Mit dem Zukunftstag bietest du potenziellen Förderpartnern eine konkrete und wirkungsvolle Möglichkeit, Jugendliche in ihrer Region zu unterstützen.

Über uns

Mit dem Zukunftstag – Dein Crashkurs fürs Leben bringen wir essenzielles Finanz- und Wirtschaftswissen an Deutschlands Schulen und schließen damit eine wichtige Lücke im Lehrplan.

Seit 2019 haben wir uns zu einer der am schnellsten wachsenden gemeinnützigen Bildungsinitiativen Deutschlands entwickelt. Bereits mehr als 200.000 Schülerinnen und Schüler haben an unseren Zukunftstagen teilgenommen.

Unser Ziel ist es, dass möglichst viele Jugendliche unabhängig von ihrer Herkunft Zugang zu lebenspraktischer Finanzbildung erhalten.

description:
Merlin bringt KI in die öffentliche Verwaltung. Mit unserer Telefon-KI, unserem Chatbot und unserem KI-Assistenten entlasten wir Rathäuser, Landratsämter und Behörden. So haben die Mitarbeitenden wieder mehr Zeit für das, was wirklich zählt, und Bürgerinnen bekommen schneller Hilfe. Nach nur 1 Jahr am Markt arbeiten bereits über 120 Kommunen in ganz Deutschland mit Merlin. Wir werden unterstützt durch erfahrene Investoren, GovTech Gründerinnen und ehemalige Spitzenpolitiker*innen.

Als Customer Success Manager (m/w/d) begleitest du unsere Kundinnen von der Vertragsphase über das Onboarding bis in den Alltag und bleibst dauerhaft ihre feste Ansprechperson. Dabei geht es um mehr als zufriedene Kundinnen: Du sorgst dafür, dass Merlin in den Verwaltungen wirklich genutzt wird. Du findest Wege, wie mehr Mitarbeitende und Ämter davon profitieren, und erkennst, wo wir noch mehr helfen können. Als erste Person im Customer Success legst du außerdem den Grundstein dafür, wie Merlin seine Kund*innen in Zukunft betreut.

Das sagt dir dein zukünftiger Manager:

Wenn es unseren Kundinnen gut geht, geht es auch uns gut. Sie sind das Wichtigste, was wir haben, und genau so behandeln wir sie auch. Mit dieser Haltung haben wir uns in kurzer Zeit einen Namen gemacht: In der kommunalen Welt kennt man Merlin inzwischen als Anbieter, der sich wirklich um seine Kundinnen kümmert. Mit dir möchte ich ein professionelles Customer-Success-Team aufbauen, das dafür sorgt, dass es so bleibt.

Tobias, Gründer & Geschäftsführer

🪴 Das wird dein Job

  • Dein eigenes Kundenportfolio: Schon ab der Vertragsphase übernimmst du die Verantwortung für deine Kund*innen und bist ab dann ihre persönliche Ansprechperson. Du begleitest sie von Tag 1 und baust in regelmäßigen Terminen langfristige Beziehungen zu ihnen auf.
  • Du sorgst dafür, dass Kund*innen bleiben: Im regelmäßigen Austausch merkst du früh, wenn etwas hakt, und steuerst gegen, bevor es zum Problem wird. Dein Ziel sind Kund*innen, die gern verlängern und uns weiterempfehlen.
  • Du erkennst, wo Merlin noch mehr helfen kann: Ob weitere Ämter, mehr Nutzer*innen oder ein weiteres Produkt, du entdeckst Potenziale und bringst Up- und Crosssells gemeinsam mit unserem Vertrieb voran.
  • Bei dir laufen die Fäden zusammen: Du bist die Schnittstelle zwischen deinen Kund*innen und unseren Teams aus Produkt, Vertrieb und Marketing. Du koordinierst, was gebraucht wird und bringst damit Merlin als Ganzes weiter.
  • Customer Success aufbauen: Du legst das Fundament für diesen Bereich: Playbook, Onboarding-Standards und Kennzahlen wie Nutzung und Verlängerungsquote. Mit unserer Kundenzahl wird auch das Team stetig wachsen, und du prägst, wie es aussieht und arbeitet.

🤗 Damit passt du zu uns

  • Du hast mindestens 2 Jahre Berufserfahrung mit viel Kundenkontakt, zum Beispiel im Customer Success, im Account Management, in der Beratung, im Projektmanagement oder in der öffentlichen Verwaltung.
  • Du kümmerst dich gern: Du bist offen und herzlich, Menschen vertrauen dir schnell, und es macht dir Freude, für andere da zu sein. Deine Kommunikationsfähigkeiten sind außergewöhnlich.
  • Du bringst technisches Verständnis mit: Du hast bereits mit erklärungsbedürftiger Software gearbeitet und kannst technische Fragen von Kund*innen verständlich beantworten. Neue Produkte verstehst du schnell bis ins Detail und denkst kreativ darüber nach, wie Verwaltungen noch mehr aus Merlin herausholen.
  • Du hast ein Gespür fürs Kaufmännische: Du erkennst Chancen und weißt, was eine gute Kundenbeziehung wert ist, ganz ohne Verkäufer-Ego.
  • Du bist strukturiert und bleibst dran: Auch bei vielen Kund*innen und Themen behältst du den Überblick und hältst, was du zusagst. Gute Abläufe aufzubauen macht dir Spaß.
  • Du gestaltest deine Arbeit mit KI: Du nutzt KI nicht nur ab und zu, sondern hast schon eigene Workflows oder Agenten gebaut und wiederkehrende Abläufe automatisiert.

💜 Warum du zu Merlin solltest

  • Arbeit mit Sinn: Mit GovTech tun wir unserem Land etwas Gutes. Jede Kommune, die du begleitest, wird ein Stück einfacher, für die Menschen, die dort arbeiten, und für alle, die auf sie angewiesen sind.
  • Du gestaltest von Anfang an: Du baust Customer Success bei Merlin auf und prägst, wohin sich der Bereich entwickelt, mit echter Verantwortung und berichtest direkt an unseren Geschäftsführer.
  • Du entwickelst dich schneller als anderswo: Du bekommst regelmäßig ehrliches Feedback und übernimmst früh echte Verantwortung. In einem ehrgeizigen Team, das Spaß an der Arbeit hat, wächst du fachlich und persönlich über dich hinaus.
  • Transparente Vergütung: 50.000–80.000 € je nach Erfahrung. Der Großteil ist fix, dazu kommt ein Bonus, der daran hängt, dass unsere Kund*innen bleiben und mit uns wachsen.
  • Hybrid in München: Unser Büro liegt im WERK1 im Werksviertel am Ostbahnhof, einem lebendigen Tech- und Startup-Hub. Einen Teil der Woche kannst du von zuhause arbeiten.
  • Corporate Benefits: Regelmäßige Team-Events, Wellpass und Offsites.
