title: Enterprise Account Executive (DACH)
description:
ChurchDesk ist die All-in-One-Plattform für die digitale Arbeit von Kirchen. Unsere Vision: Kirchen die Freiheit zu geben, sich auf das Wesentliche zu konzentrieren – auf Menschen und Gemeinschaft statt auf Verwaltung. Dafür bündeln wir in einer Lösung, die speziell für kirchliche Strukturen entwickelt wurde, alles, was Kirchen in ganz Europa für ihre tägliche Arbeit brauchen: von CRM, Mitgliederverwaltung und Kalender über Spendenmanagement und Website-Verwaltung bis hin zu einer eigenen Social App und mehr als zehn weiteren Modulen.

Mit Büros in Berlin, Kopenhagen, Oslo und Groningen sind wir ein internationales Team, das Technologie und gesellschaftliche Wirkung verbindet. Bereits über 10.000 Kirchengemeinden in Europa vertrauen auf ChurchDesk.

Warum Du Teil unserer Erfolgsgeschichte werden solltest?

Kirchen stehen mitten in einem tiefgreifenden Wandel – und immer mehr große kirchliche Organisationen setzen dabei auf ChurchDesk. Unser Enterprise-Geschäft im DACH-Raum steht auf einem starken Fundament. Als Enterprise Account Executive sorgst Du dafür, dass es weiter wächst: Du überzeugst (Erz-)Bistümer, Diözesen, Landeskirchen und kirchliche Verbände von ChurchDesk und führst sie vom ersten Gespräch bis zur Unterschrift. Eine Rolle mit viel Gestaltungsspielraum, echter Verantwortung und einer Wirkung, die weit über Zahlen hinausgeht.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du gewinnst neue Enterprise-Kunden im DACH-Raum durch gezielte Outbound-Aktivitäten, die Bearbeitung von Inbound-Leads und den Aufbau eines starken Netzwerks in der kirchlichen Landschaft.

  • Du führst komplexe Sales-Zyklen eigenständig – von Prospecting und Bedarfsanalyse über Präsentationen bis hin zu Verhandlung und Abschluss.

  • Du verstehst die Strukturen und Herausforderungen großer kirchlicher Organisationen und entwickelst passgenaue Lösungen, die echten Mehrwert schaffen.

  • Du navigierst souverän durch Organisationen mit vielen Beteiligten – von Leitungsebenen über Fachabteilungen bis zu Gremien.

  • Du pflegst eine gesunde Pipeline, erstellst verlässliche Forecasts und übernimmst Verantwortung für Dein eigenes Umsatzziel.

  • Du arbeitest eng mit Customer Success, Produkt und Marketing zusammen und sorgst für eine reibungslose Übergabe neuer Kunden.

  • Du vertrittst ChurchDesk professionell bei Kundenterminen vor Ort, auf Fachkonferenzen und gegenüber hochrangigen kirchlichen Entscheidungsträgern.


  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung im B2B-Vertrieb, idealerweise als Account Executive mit Fokus auf Enterprise-Kunden im SaaS-Umfeld.

  • Du hast bereits erfolgreich Neukunden gewonnen und weißt, wie man auch in längeren, komplexen Sales-Zyklen ans Ziel kommt.

  • Erfahrung im Vertrieb an stakeholder-getriebene Organisationen, idealerweise im kirchlichen, NGO- oder öffentlichen Umfeld.

  • Ausgeprägte Kommunikations-, Präsentations- und Verhandlungskompetenz – auch auf Führungs- und Leitungsebene.

  • Du fühlst Dich in HubSpot zu Hause und nutzt es, um Deine Pipeline strukturiert im Blick zu behalten.

  • Verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse, sehr gute Englischkenntnisse sowie Reisebereitschaft innerhalb des DACH-Raums.

  • Eine proaktive, ergebnisorientierte Arbeitsweise und Interesse an der Mission von ChurchDesk und der Rolle der Kirche in einer sich wandelnden Gesellschaft.

Was wir Dir bieten

  • Eine Rolle in einem wachsenden Tech-Unternehmen, in der du echte Verantwortung übernimmst, deine Arbeit aktiv mitgestaltest und dabei viel dazulernst.

  • Wachse mit uns: Ein dedizierter Sales Coach an deiner Seite sowie die Möglichkeit, dich durch Kurse und Webinare technisch und im Pre-Sales stetig weiterzuentwickeln.

  • Zukunft im Blick – Wir bezuschussen deine betriebliche Altersvorsorge mit 20 %, damit du heute gut arbeitest und morgen gut abgesichert bist.

  • 30 Tage Urlaub – weil ausreichend Erholung wichtig ist.

  • 37 Stunden Arbeitswoche – mehr Balance, mehr Zeit für dich.

  • Eine offene und ehrliche Feedbackkultur – gemeinsam wachsen, voneinander lernen, transparent kommunizieren.

  • Ein wunderschönes, modernes Altbau-Office im Herzen Neukölln – zentral, lebendig und perfekt angebunden. 

  • Lust auf einen Tapetenwechsel? Besuche uns in Kopenhagen, Oslo oder Groningen! Wir übernehmen deine Reise- und Spesenkosten.

  • Unvergessliche Team-Erlebnisse – von Company Events bis zu gemeinsamen Reisen nach Kroatien & Prag.

Über ChurchDesk

Bei ChurchDesk sind wir der Meinung, dass die Kirche eine wichtige Rolle in der Gesellschaft spielt. Unsere Plattform wird von Tausenden von Gemeinden genutzt, um ihre Arbeit zu organisieren, die Kommunikation mit Mitgliedern zu verbessern, mehr Menschen zu erreichen und neue Möglichkeiten der Mittelbeschaffung zu erschließen.
Unsere Kunden sind Teil einer der größten und ältesten Institutionen der Welt: der Kirche. Sie befindet sich in einem erheblichen Wandel, um sich auf die Zukunft vorzubereiten – und wir sind hier, um diese Transformation zu unterstützen. Für Kirchen in ganz Europa ist es entscheidend, effizienter zu arbeiten und mit ihren Mitgliedern und Gemeinden in Verbindung zu bleiben.

ChurchDesk gibt es seit mehr als 15 Jahren – von einem Startup zu einem internationalen Unternehmen, das Kunden in ganz Europa bedient. Und wir fangen gerade erst an!

Wir leben unsere Werte aktiv in unserer täglichen Arbeit:

#challenge: Wir fordern uns selbst – und unsere Kunden – kontinuierlich heraus, uns zu verbessern. Wir arbeiten wie ein professionelles Sportteam: mit Ehrgeiz, Disziplin und starkem Teamgeist.

#dogoodbusiness: Gutes Geschäft zu machen ist ein Marathon, kein Sprint. Es erfordert Ausdauer, Qualität und Integrität – jeden einzelnen Tag.

#jointheride: Die Reise ist genauso wichtig wie das Ziel. Seien Sie ein Teil davon, feiern Sie Erfolge – und haben Sie Spaß! Wir schätzen es, zusammen zu sein, besonders im Büro.

description:
Distribusion is the world’s leading ground transportation marketplace and gives travelers seamless access to ground transportation online, from search to ticket purchase. We have built a cutting-edge B2B technology platform that connects bus, rail, and ferry operators in 70+ countries with the biggest online retailers, including Google Maps and Booking.com.
We are shaping the future of travel and building the largest global network of transport providers and retailers. We are one of the fastest growing startups in travel, backed by leading VCs (TQ Ventures, Lightrock, Creandum and Northzone), and now, following our recent $80m Series C funding, we are ready to push beyond.

Distribusion is quickly expanding globally and looking for a (Senior) Technical Partnerships Manager to join the Corporate Travel Partnerships team to drive the strategic growth and performance of some of our key partnerships in the business travel space. This role will require you to wear many hats and certainly not leave you bored!

What you will do:

  • Support Pre-Sales: Act as a technical expert during initial engagements to evaluate partner needs and demonstrate our capabilities.

  • Consult on API Implementation: Guide partners through their API integration, ensuring a seamless process that meets certification standards.

  • Translate Requirements: Gather technical requirements directly from external partners and break them down into actionable specs for internal teams.

  • Manage Custom Projects: Drive the end-to-end delivery of custom developments, managing timelines, stakeholders, and go-live execution

  • Guide Product Development: Leverage partner feedback and insights to shape the ongoing development of our core API and integration tools.

  • Manage Technical Relationships: Own the long-term technical relationship with partners to drive collaboration, product engagement, and brand stickiness.

Workplace: We are mainly looking for this role based in Germany, preferably at our headquarters in Berlin.
We are a remote-first company, with teams around the Globe and our HQ office in Berlin, where the team often meets in the office.


Who you are:

  • 5 + years of work experience in a tech company (experience in a technology/software company, travel agency, transportation, and logistics industry is an advantage but not a must). 

  • You have had deep exposure to API integrations, and you are confident in navigating documentation, sprint cycles, and system architecture, even if you’re not the one coding.

  • A big plus if you have experience in the corporate travel space (any vertical).

  • You’re a structured communicator who can translate complexity into clarity for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • You take ownership, thrive in ambiguity, and are energised by solving cross-functional coordination challenges.

  • You’re fluent in English, both written and spoken. Other languages are a plus.

  • You’re open to business travel, as needed.

What you can expect:

  • You will join a fast-paced travel tech company and take on a rapidly growing industry.

  • You will take on ownership and responsibility from day one and have a direct impact on the success of the company.

  • We value agility! We’re constantly updating our tech stack and offer the best possible tools to ensure all of our in-house engineers, partners, and carriers benefit from cutting-edge, efficient solutions.

  • You will work with global companies. Our product attracts the biggest names in travel technology, such as Booking.com, Google Maps, and national carriers like Amtrak, Deutsche Bahn, Renfe, and SNCF.

  • You will join an international team of talented and driven people with a clear mission. Expect your colleagues to inspire, support and challenge you every day!

  • We offer flexible and remote working conditions, relocation opportunities, and career growth in a small and developing company.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer

What you'll bring

title: Implementation Specialist
description:
About Us 

Hawk is the leading provider of AI-supported anti-money laundering and fraud detection technology. Banks and payment providers globally are using Hawk’s powerful combination of traditional rules and explainable AI to improve the effectiveness of their AML compliance and fraud prevention by identifying more crime while maximizing efficiency by reducing false positives. With our solution, we are playing a vital role in the global fight against Money Laundering, Fraud, or the financing of terrorism. We offer a culture of mutual trust, support and passion – while providing individuals with opportunities to grow professionally and make a difference in the world. 

Your Mission

As an Implementation Specialist at Hawk, your responsibility is to transform customer requirements into a functioning solution that helps them achieve their business objectives around transaction monitoring, customer screening and fraud detection, alongside cutting-edge AI technologies. You start with a signed contract and support the customer until go-live. This includes translating policies, regulatory obligations and risk factors into Hawk's setup, data mapping, workflow configuration, UAT support and ensuring that key project timelines and milestones are met. You support our customers in realising true value by detecting more financial crime, allowing investigators to focus on what matters instead of drowning in false positives, and adopting state-of-the-art AI technologies.

Key Responsibilities

  • Requirements and needs assessment: gather and analyse the customer's AML, fraud and screening requirements and advise on best-practice configuration.

  • Configuration: translate policies, screening algorithms, regulatory requirements and risk factors into Hawk's setup, covering rules, screening, customer risk rating and workflows.

  • Data mapping and integration: lead the technical deployment and integration with the customer's systems, via API or batch mechanisms.

  • Testing and go-live: support the customer through testing, UAT and sign-off, troubleshoot issues, and support a successful transition to a production environment.

  • Training and enablement: deliver training to the customer's teams from a functional as well as technical standpoint.

  • Project management: plan and run the implementation from signature to go-live on time and within scope, with documentation and regular stakeholder updates, combining hands-on work with project leadership.

  • Primary contact: be the first point of contact for implementation questions and issues.

  • Collaboration and feedback: work closely with Customer Value Partners for a smooth implementation, and bring actionable customer feedback and gaps to Product, Development and Hawk's GTM organisation.

  • Document every configuration decision and the reasoning behind it, so the setup holds up when the customer's auditor or regulator asks why a rule was set the way it was.

  • Manage each implementation task and the implementation success as an outcome you own, as directed by our Customer Value Partner, resulting in activity completion and a go-live on the dates you committed to.

Your Profile

  • 6+ years in implementation consulting or solution consulting, with at least 3 of those years hands-on implementing AML, fraud or screening solutions.

  • Subject matter expertise in AML and compliance. You are familiar with key typologies and patterns, the regulatory expectations behind them, and how monitoring programmes as well as AI get examined.

  • You can confidently stand in front of an MLRO and discuss and defend a rule set. This is a must-have, not a nice-to-have.

  • Hands-on data skills: SQL, APIs, CSV and JSON, and data modelling. You're familiar with standardised payment message formats, including SWIFT MT and ISO 20022, SEPA and card data.

  • Integration literacy. You don't write production code, but you're at home with APIs, JSON payloads, SFTP configurations as well as SSO.

  • Proven track record of taking complex implementations to go-live on time, ideally several in parallel, with banking customers or other financial institutions.

  • Stakeholder alignment. You ensure that internal and external parties both have the information they need, keep them aligned and manage expectations.

  • Able to explain complexity simply. Imagine data models for compliance leads, fraud typologies for data engineers. You do it clearly in writing and in the room, in fluent English.

  • A degree in computer science, information systems, engineering, finance or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Bonus

  • Business-fluent German, for working with our DACH customers.

  • CAMS (or equivalent) certification, or time spent in a second-line compliance or MLRO team.

  • Builds constructive relationships with customers and stays calm and under pressure Builder mentality: works independently and brings structure to ambiguity where no established process exists, taking the initiative to define one.

  • Is a resourceful problem-solver who investigates unknowns and tests system behaviour. Knows when and whom to escalate.

  • Manages expectations proactively. Flags timeline and scope risks early, quantifies them, offers phased options and aligns Sales and Customer Success.

  • Handles product gaps transparently. Clarifies the underlying (regulatory) requirement, offers workarounds with their trade-offs, feeds back to Product and doesn't commit to unconfirmed dates .

  • You use AI tools such as Claude in your daily workflow to speed up mapping, documentation and analysis, and you have opinions about where they help and where they don't.

title: Senior Financial Systems Engineer (m/f/d)
description:
We're building a new global Berlitz, and this is your opportunity to help shape it. Nearly 150 years of expertise, meeting the ambition and technology to power a new era of learning.

If you are the kind of person who thrives in a fast-paced environment, isn’t afraid of a blank page, and is excited to help shape the future of a global company undergoing a significant transformation, you might belong at Berlitz!

About the role

Berlitz is rebuilding its commercial and financial platform. That includes a new CRM, usage-based billing, modern payment processing, and a consolidated ERP, all supporting new digital products for learners, teachers, and enterprise customers.

We're looking for a Senior Financial Systems Engineer to own the flow of money through that platform, from quote and checkout through billing and payment to the general ledger. You'll be the technical authority on how our systems exchange financial data. You'll make sure every customer, invoice, payment, refund, and credit reconciles cleanly at month-end.

This is a hands-on engineering role that sits at the intersection of engineering and finance. You'll report into Engineering and work day to day with Finance, RevOps, and our external NetSuite implementation partner.

What you'll do

  • Own the architecture and data contracts for our order-to-cash flow across HubSpot, Stripe, Adyen, Metronome, and NetSuite.

  • Build and maintain integrations using NetSuite SuiteScript and REST/SuiteTalk, PSP APIs and webhooks, and our iPaaS (Workato), choosing custom code or low-code where each makes sense.

  • Design reconciliation between payment processors, billing, bank settlements, and the ledger, and build the jobs, alerts, and audit trails that keep it reliable.

  • Model prepaid credit packages and usage-based consumption correctly, including deferred revenue, drawdown, expiry, refunds, and credit notes.

  • Support multi-entity, multi-currency operations, including subsidiaries, intercompany flows, FX, and tax handling.

  • Act as the technical counterpart to our NetSuite implementation partner: review designs, challenge assumptions, and take ownership of what they build.

  • Partner with Finance to shorten and de-risk month-end close by removing manual work and fixing data quality at the source.

  • Document the financial data model and integrations so the platform is supportable beyond you.

What you'll bring

  • 6+ years in software engineering, with at least 3 years building or owning financial, billing, or payments systems.

  • Hands-on NetSuite development experience (SuiteScript 2.x, REST/SuiteTalk, saved searches) and a solid understanding of its record model, including customers, sales orders, invoices, payments, deposits, and journals.

  • Production experience integrating Stripe and/or Adyen, including webhooks, idempotency, payouts and settlement reports, disputes, and fees.

  • Real accounting literacy. You can explain revenue recognition, deferred revenue, cash application, and bank reconciliation, and you know why they matter to Finance.

  • Strong integration engineering fundamentals: API design, event-driven patterns, retries and error handling, and data validation.

  • Comfort working across teams and translating between engineers, accountants, and commercial stakeholders.

  • Good judgement under deadline pressure, with the ability to ship pragmatically without creating reconciliation debt.

Nice to have

  • Experience with usage-based or consumption billing platforms (Metronome, Orb, Chargebee, or similar).

  • Experience with HubSpot, Salesforce, or other CRM-to-ERP integrations.

  • iPaaS experience (Workato, Boomi, Celigo, MuleSoft).

  • Experience migrating from a legacy billing or CRM system to a new stack.

  • Exposure to SOC 2 / ISO 27001 controls around financial systems.

  • Experience at a multi-country business or in education / subscription services.

What success looks like

  • First 90 days: You understand our current order-to-cash flows end to end. You've taken technical ownership of the payments-to-ledger integration and identified the biggest reconciliation risks.

  • First 6 months: New products bill, collect, and post to NetSuite correctly across entities and currencies. Month-end reconciliation between PSPs and the ledger is largely automated.

  • First year: Our financial systems are well documented, monitored, and trusted by Finance, and they're ready to scale to new products and markets.

Why Berlitz

  • A rare chance to shape a financial platform nearly from scratch at a global brand with a long history.

  • Direct impact on how the company operates and reports, with high visibility across Engineering, Finance, and leadership.

  • A team that values pragmatic engineering and cross-functional ownership.

At Berlitz, connecting people across languages and cultures is at the heart of what we do. Our global workplace reflects the diverse world we serve, bringing together different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. We create an inclusive environment where everyone has an equal opportunity to belong, contribute and grow.

Ready to shape what’s next? Join us and help build the future with us.

title: Staff Backend Engineer - Search Features & APIs (SABR)
description:
About us

Launched in 2019, Constructor is an AI-first e-commerce search and discovery platform that helps shoppers find the right products at the right time and enables leading global e-commerce brands to drive meaningful revenue and conversion gains.

About the team

The SABR team owns the top layer of request processing for product discovery. We own the service that first receives product discovery requests (autocomplete, search, browse & recommendations) & executes the entire business logic that drives product discovery. That service also functions as a gateway to parse incoming user requests, orchestrate calls across the internal services that do the ranking and retrieval, interpret their responses, and assemble the final response the customer sees. We also own the public configuration APIs customers use to control how discovery behaves, and the MCP layer that exposes all of it to AI agents.

Our team owns both platform & product components: Because of the positioning of our services, we take part in every architectural decision of our core product offering. At the same time, our goals are heavily influenced by direct customer feedback, because all product discovery-related features are either implemented in or integrated with our services.

All of our services are public APIs, so interface design and backward compatibility are a constant part of the job. But most of our attention goes to keeping them fast and up: we serve up to 15k RPS, fan out to many internal services on every request, and are expected to stay available and degrade gracefully when any of them fails or slows down.

The work is distributed systems in practice rather than in theory: request orchestration, failure isolation, caching, latency budgets, capacity planning, and the observability to know what is actually happening in production. The team is small enough that engineers own problems end to end, from design through on-call.

About you

You're a staff-level engineer who wants to own systems, not tickets. You've built high-traffic, low-latency Python services and carried the pager for them. You think in trade-offs: latency versus cost, flexibility versus a public API that customers can't afford to see break, the fix that ships this week versus the architecture that has to last two years. You can lead work that spans several engineers and several quarters, you enjoy mentoring others, and you're fine when a problem shows up half-defined. You don't mind being the one who reads the spec for some unfamiliar protocol, works out how it fits, and designs an integration that holds up at scale. You change your mind when someone has a better argument, you make the people around you better, and you still care about your code long after it merges.

What you will do

  • Own the technical direction of one or more of our services - architecture, performance, and reliability.

  • Lead design of new systems and public APIs, and the evolution of existing ones as traffic and feature scope grow.

  • Raise the engineering bar through design and code review, and mentor mid and senior engineers into owning bigger scopes.

  • Partner with product, other engineering teams, and solutions/support to shape what we build and to represent search constraints and trade-offs honestly.

  • Take part in on-call for the systems you own, and lead incident response and follow-through when things break.

What we are looking for

Technical

  • Substantial experience building and operating high-traffic, low-latency backend services in production.

  • Extensive Python knowledge (our primary language).

  • Experience with observability and performance work in live systems.

  • Experience designing and evolving public APIs that external customers depend on.

  • Experience designing & implementing scalable service-oriented architectures.

Beyond the code

title: Senior Backend Engineer - ClickPipes Platform
description:
About the Team

The ClickPipes team builds the services that power data ingestion into ClickHouse Cloud. As a primary entry point for customers’ data, ClickPipes is critical to product adoption and the company’s growth. We work at petabyte scale, solving challenges in distributed systems, fault tolerance, and high-throughput ingestion. You’ll help make these pipelines performant, reliable, and easy to operate, with ownership of technical decisions and the platform as a whole.

You can find some of the team’s recent work highlighted in our blog:

  • GCP Pub/Sub connector for ClickPipes is now in Private Preview

  • Terraform & OpenAPI for ClickPipes is now Generally Available

  • Unordered mode for GCS ClickPipes is now available

We’re looking for backend engineers with experience in data-intensive systems who enjoy working across technologies. You’ll collaborate with engineering and product partners and drive projects from design through production.

What will you do?

  • Build and evolve integrations with streaming platforms and object storage, including Kafka, Kinesis, Pub/Sub, S3, GCS, and Azure Blob Storage.

  • Continuously improve our systems based on operational metrics, customer feedback, and evolving business requirements.

  • Drive technical discussions and contribute to architectural decisions that impact our platform's scalability and resilience.

  • Participate in on-call rotations to ensure system reliability and respond to production incidents.

About you:

  • 5+ years of software development experience building and operating distributed systems.

  • Strong knowledge of Go and its ecosystem.

  • Experience designing systems for scalability and fault tolerance, with an understanding of concurrency, consistency, and failure recovery.

  • Understanding of cloud-native architecture and practical experience with at least one major cloud provider.

  • Experience diagnosing and resolving production issues in distributed systems.

  • Ability to communicate technical ideas clearly and collaborate across engineering and product teams.

  • Experience with data ingestion pipelines, streaming platforms, or object storage is a plus.

Perks

  • Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

  • Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

  • Equity in the company - Every new eligible team member who joins our company receives equity.

  • Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

  • A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

  • Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here. Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.

Equal Opportunity & Privacy

title: Senior Avionics System Engineer
description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecraft for humanity.

About the Role

The Exploration Company builds the TEC vehicle family and is preparing the next generation of vehicles and products. As a Senior Avionics Engineer in the Future Systems team, you will be the system engineer who turns future mission concepts into credible, well-defined avionics, communications and power architectures. You will bring a solid working expertise in electrical power systems, data handling and communications, and you will shape designs that are ready to be challenged, tested and flown.

You will work closely with the other engineering disciplines, and you will report to the Principal Engineer of the project.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own work packages or full future projects in avionics, communications and power, from concept through verification, delivering on time, on quality and on cost.

  • Define functional breakdowns and high-level requirements, flow them down to avionics subsystems, and manage the associated technical baselines so the design meets the needs of each project.

  • Develop system architectures and conceptual designs, perform avionics-related technical trade-offs, and carry out budget and performance analyses (power, mass, data, thermal interfaces).

  • Write development, implementation, verification and validation plans, and drive them through to completion with the teams involved.

  • Develop hardware solutions for future projects, from requirements to integration and test support.

What we would love to see from you

In this role, ideally, you will have the following:

  • Proven hands-on experience in designing electrical systems for spacecraft or other aerospace platforms, with a clear record of delivering them.

  • A broad understanding of the full functional chain of space-based avionics, communications and power systems, and how the pieces interact.

  • Able to work effectively with neighboring subsystems (thermal, GNC, propulsion, flight software, operations), understanding their interfaces and constraints well enough to resolve cross-disciplinary trade-offs and keep interface control documents aligned.

  • Strong systems engineering skills: defining requirements and their flow-down, managing technical baselines, and producing architectures and trade-offs.

  • Experience with budgets and performance analysis (power, mass, data, thermal) to support design decisions.

  • Hands-on experience with development, assembly, integration and testing of electrical units for space applications.

  • Strong written and oral communication skills in English, with the ability to explain technical issues clearly to engineers, managers and partners.

  • A degree in Electrical Engineering, Telecommunications, Aerospace Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience in the relevant domain.

As a guideline, candidates typically bring 5+ years of relevant experience in aerospace system design. We value demonstrated capability over the number of years, so we welcome applications from candidates with a strong track record who may have followed a non-linear path.

Skills and Behaviours

  • Analytical and problem-solving mindset, with the ability to structure complex problems and reach sound decisions.

  • Organised and pragmatic, able to set priorities across several work packages.

  • Positive and flexible, with a can-do attitude to get the job done.

  • Collaborative, communicating at all levels of the business and working across disciplines.

  • Feedback ready, willing to give proactive and mindful feedback across all levels of the company.

  • Highly motivated, to work in a fast-paced, autonomously driven and demanding start-up environment.

Why you should join us!

What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:  

  • We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind 

  • We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them  

  • We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?  

We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. Please submit your CV now for immediate consideration and we will be in touch shortly.

  • Take technical ownership of the spacecraft's navigation sensor suite, including requirements definition, architecture, component selection, and system-level performance.

Key Responsibilities

As a Fluid Systems Development Engineer, your responsibilities will include:

  • Translate engine-level functional and performance requirements into fluid-system requirements, architectures, and development priorities.

  • Lead architecture trade-off studies, sensitivity analyses, and risk assessments to support robust design decisions.

  • Define and manage the development roadmap for fluid-system sub-assemblies, from concept through maturation and qualification.

  • Lead the design of fluid systems and the selection, development, and integration of their components, including make-or-buy decisions.

  • Define and manage the verification and validation strategy, including requirements, test specifications, acceptance criteria, and evidence of compliance.

  • Design and specify the pneumatic equipment required to support demonstrator test campaigns and test-article operations.

  • Feed test results and lessons learned back into system design, requirements, and future development activities.


What we would love to see from you

  • Minimum 2 years of proven experience developing propulsion fluid systems

Dazu kommt eine riesige Datenbasis: Fast alle Kund:innen sind registriert und haben ein eigenes Profil. Du entwickelst die Logik für dynamische, hochgradig segmentierte Kommunikation über alle Kanäle – von der Foodji App über In-App-Messages, Push und Mail bis zum Foodji Screen direkt am Gerät – und nutzt Daten, um sie kontinuierlich weiterzuentwickeln.

Deine Mission bei Foodji

  • Du legst das analytische und konzeptionelle Fundament für eine skalierbare CRM- und Lifecycle-Funktion für unsere B2C-Kund:innen.

  • Von der Hypothese über Segmentierung und Testdesign bis zur Auswertung von A/B-Tests und Kohorten: Du definierst, was wir ausprobieren, misst, was wirkt, und iterierst schnell auf Basis der Ergebnisse.

  • Welche Events lösen welche Kommunikation aus? Du definierst sie auf Basis unserer Daten, konzipierst dynamische Segmente und Journeys, die Stocklevels, Produktkombinationen und Nutzerbedürfnisse berücksichtigen, und entscheidest datenbasiert, ob App, In-App, Push, Mail oder Foodji Screen der richtige Kanal ist.

  • In Snowflake und mit KI-Tools wie Claude analysierst du Daten eigenständig, findest die relevanten Hebel und priorisierst Maßnahmen nach ihrem erwarteten Impact.

  • Mit Marketing, Product, Revenue Management und BI arbeitest du eng zusammen und machst Daten und technische Möglichkeiten für CRM nutzbar. Dem Team, das Kampagnen und Content umsetzt, lieferst du Segmente, Journey-Konzepte und klare Briefings.

  • Du verantwortest Datenqualität und Governance deiner Segmente, Events und Systeme und stellst sicher, dass alles performant, sicher und datenschutzkonform läuft.

  • Du baust unser CRM komplett neu auf und übernimmst die Projektverantwortung für die Integration in unsere System- und Datenlandschaft, von der Anforderungsdefinition bis zum Go-live. Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Braze oder vergleichbare Plattformen kennst du so gut, dass deine Konzepte direkt umsetzbar sind.

Das bringst du mit

  • Mindestens 3 Jahre Erfahrung in CRM Analytics, Data Analytics, Lifecycle Marketing oder einem vergleichbaren Bereich.

  • Ausgeprägter Datenblick: Du arbeitest sicher mit Daten in Snowflake oder vergleichbaren Data Warehouses, baust komplexe Segmente und Kohorten und leitest daraus klare Maßnahmen ab.

  • Analytics first: Rund 60 bis 70 Prozent deiner Arbeit sind für dich Analytics. Du iterierst schnell über Hypothesen, A/B-Tests und Kohortenanalysen, statt lange an der perfekten Gestaltung zu feilen.

  • Du bist komplett KI-enabled: Tools wie Claude oder MCP nutzt du ganz selbstverständlich in deinem Arbeitsalltag.

  • Gute Kenntnisse in Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Braze oder einer vergleichbaren CRM-Plattform: Du weißt, was technisch möglich ist, und konzipierst Segmente und Journeys entsprechend. Ein Plus ist Erfahrung mit Omnichannel-Journeys über App, Push, In-App und Mail.

  • Technisches Verständnis und Lust auf enge Zusammenarbeit mit Product: Du kennst die Abläufe zwischen CRM-Systemen, Plattformen und Datenquellen und achtest auf Performance, Sicherheit und Datenschutz.

  • Erfahrung im Aufbau oder in der Einführung eines CRM-Systems: Du übernimmst Ownership, treibst die Integration als Projekt eigenverantwortlich voran und koordinierst die beteiligten Teams und Dienstleister.

  • Sichere Kommunikation auf Deutsch oder Englisch in Wort und Schrift.

DAS BIETEN WIR DIR

  • Office Foodji & Lunchit App: Immer bestens versorgt

  • bAV: Mit der Degura Pension Cloud sichern und bezuschussen wir jetzt schon deine Rente

  • Spendit Card: Wir stocken dein Gehalt auf! Mit Spendit stehen dir bis zu fünfzig Euro netto im Monat on top zur freien Verfügung

  • EGYM Wellpass: Mit uns bleibst du fit & wir bringen dich in die angesagtesten Fitness- und Wellnessstudios

  • JobRad: Spring mit uns aufs Rad und lease dir dein Traumrad oder Pedelec

  • KITA/Kiga Kostenzuschuss: Wir bezuschussen deine Kosten für die Kinderbetreuung, damit deine Kinder immer bestens versorgt sind

  • Mitarbeiterrabatte: Du erhältst attraktive Promotions und Discounts verschiedener Brands

  • Food Tastings: Teste dich mit unserem Foodteam durch unsere Produkte und gestalte unser Sortiment von morgen

  • Development: Deine Weiterentwicklung liegt uns am Herzen und mit regelmäßigen Feedbackgesprächen und Trainings bieten wir dir spannende Perspektiven!

  • Flexwork: Arbeite 30 Tage im Jahr aus dem EU-Ausland

  • Top Office Lage: Genieße eine erstklassige Arbeitsumgebung im Münchener Glockenbachviertel mit der Isar vor der Tür

  • Team Events: Wir sind ein Team - beim Skiday, Frühstück, Culture Week oder Office Party feiern wir gemeinsam!

NOCH FRAGEN?

Wir freuen uns auf deine Nachricht und helfen dir gerne weiter!

Hi, schön, dass du da bist! Wir sind Foodji - ein Team aus Food-Lovern & Tech-Nerds.

Unsere Mission ist es, frisches, gesundes und vor allem leckeres Essen überall dort anzubieten, wo Menschen den Großteil ihres Alltags verbringen – in Büros, ganz gleich, ob im Gewerbegebiet oder mitten in der Stadt, während langer Schichten im Krankenhaus oder in den Tiefen einer Produktionshalle, in der rund um die Uhr Menschen arbeiten. Überall bieten wir vollwertige Gerichte, Snacks und Getränke genau dort an, wo und wann du sie brauchst.

Wir wollen einen positiven Effekt erzielen – auf die Umwelt, den Alltag unserer Kund:innen und unsere Communities. Deshalb spenden wir übrig gebliebene Gerichte an Foodsharing und andere soziale Initiativen direkt vor unserer Haustür.

Als Marktführer versorgen wir mit Foodji bereits täglich Tausende Menschen in ganz Deutschland. Zu unseren Kund:innen zählen unter anderem der Münchner Flughafen, Klarna, Enpal und Wingcopter. Und wir fangen gerade erst an: Allein in Deutschland gibt es mehr als 100.000 relevante Standorte für uns.

Trage auch du deinen Teil dazu bei und bewirb dich jetzt.

title: Working Student
description:
Novaspace is seeking a Working Student to join our Munich office, supporting our team across a diverse range of consulting, innovation advisory and business activities in the space sector.

title: Operations delivery lead - Pension
description:
Location: Bath or Edinburgh - Hybrid with two days a week in our Manvers Street or George Street office

About us

Seccl is the Octopus-owned embedded investment platform, on a mission to help more people invest, and invest well.

We’re building the infrastructure behind the next generation of investing. Our technology already powers some of the UK’s most ambitious fintechs, banks, financial advisers and wealth firms, with close to a million investors relying on Seccl-powered platforms. And we’re now expanding into Europe.

We’ve got a proven product, strong momentum and big ambitions for what comes next: helping more household-name brands launch and scale investment propositions, entering new markets and replacing outdated investment infrastructure with technology that’s faster, simpler and built for scale.

We’re proud to be part of Octopus, one of the UK’s most successful privately held investment and technology groups. That gives us the backing and long-term perspective to build something substantial, while keeping the pace and energy of a high-growth business. Seccl and Octopus are both B Corp certified and share a belief that profit and purpose should go hand in hand.

If you want to help shape the future of investing in the UK and across Europe, you’ll be in good company.

Check out the Seccl website to see what we’re building and read more about our mission to shape the future of investments.

The role

We're looking for an experienced operations delivery lead to join our Pensions operations team at an exciting stage of growth.

This role will lead the operational delivery of Seccl's SIPP and ISA products. You'll be responsible for building the operational structure, processes and controls required to support a growing tax wrappers operation, ensuring we can scale efficiently whilst continuing to deliver excellent customer outcomes. A key part of the role will be working with product and engineering teams to design and embed scalable operational processes that align with the specific regulatory requirements of tax wrappers, ensuring robust controls are built into the operating model from the outset.

Reporting to the head of payments & reporting, you'll lead a specialist team of operations analysts focused on pensions and tax wrappers. Partnering closely with product, engineering and technical services, you'll have genuine scope to own, redesign and implement new ways of working to deliver operational excellence. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who enjoys solving complex operational challenges, building high-performing teams and creating scalable processes from the ground up.

What you’ll own

  • Own end-to-end performance of SIPP and ISA operations tax wrappers team

  • Lead, coach and scale a growing team of operations specialists, building a culture of ownership and client-first delivery

  • Ensure delivery of operational SLAs, SLOs and customer outcomes across all SIPP and ISA processes

  • Build workforce planning, capacity forecasting and resource models to support volume growth

  • Drive operational readiness for new client onboarding and product launches

  • Act as escalation point for incidents, coordinating response, communications, root cause analysis and lasting fixes

  • Support regulatory reporting activities and ensure appropriate operational oversight

  • Partner with Product/Engineering to improve workflows, automate where possible, enhance controls and reduce operational risk at scale

  • Create a culture of continuous improvement, accountability and operational excellence

This role’s for you if you have...

  • Operational leadership experience within platforms, wealth management or fintechs

  • Have a track record of delivering improvements by partnering with Product/Engineering/Risk to strengthen controls and enable scale

  • Experience leading and developing operational teams through periods of growth and change

  • Demonstrable experience designing scalable operational processes and operating models

  • SIPP operational expertise with an understanding of pension administration processes

  • Strong understanding of how the regulatory environment shapes pension and investment operations, including Consumer Duty, CASS, pension and ISA-specific regulatory obligations

  • Thrive in complexity and exceptions: calm, decisive, and client-focused when issues arise

  • Data-driven mindset with experience using MI and operational metrics to drive decisions

  • Communicate confidently and influence stakeholders across teams and external partners

This role isn’t for you if...

  • You rely on lots of top-down direction. You'll have freedom and ownership here - and we'll expect you to shape your own progression.

  • You're not comfortable working at pace. Things move quickly; you'll need to act decisively and think on your feet.

  • You struggle to follow through. We value people who do what they say they'll do - and who turn good ideas into real change.

What’s in it for you…

We offer a generous mix of benefits for the things that really matter to our people, including:

  • 💰 A salary between £50,000 and £70,000 reviewed annually, plus a 6% employer pension contribution and life assurance

  • 🌴 27 days’ holiday plus bank holidays, your birthday off and paid dependant leave

  • 💙 Two volunteering days each year

  • 🌎 The option to work abroad for up to six weeks a year

  • 🌟 Secclbrate, our recognition programme offering flexible rewards including extra pay, additional holiday and increased learning budget

  • 🏅 One-month paid sabbatical after eight years

  • 🏥 Private medical insurance with AXA Health

  • 👪 Enhanced parental leave

  • 💻 MacBook and up to £500 towards your home office set-up

  • 📖 Annual learning budget

  • 🌻 Health and wellbeing support, including free therapy through Wellness Cloud and mental health support through Headspace

  • 🌱 Financial wellbeing benefits, including Octopus Money, the Octopus Share Incentive Plan and will writing through Octopus Legacy

  • 🎁 Perkbox, with flexible points and a range of discounts and perks

  • 🚲 Access to Cycle to Work and Octopus Electric Vehicle Leasing

Our culture

We put people first and try hard to create an environment where people feel trusted, heard and able to do their best work.

We value openness, curiosity and different perspectives. You'll have the freedom to challenge how things are done, experiment with better ways of working and take real ownership of your impact.

Check out our Glassdoor page for the latest reviews or our LinkedIn for company updates and insights from the team.

Interview process

Interviewing is a two-way process. Our interviews are conversational, with plenty of time for you to get to know us and ask questions too.

Following an initial chat with our talent team, you can expect the process to look like:

  • First stage – 45 mins competencies-based interview with two of our operations leads

  • Second stage – one-hour technical interview or assessment with the hiring manager

  • Final stage – 45 mins bar-raiser culture-based interview

We review applications as they come in and may close the role once we have enough candidates to move forward. We’ll keep you updated throughout.

Everyone’s welcome

We want to build a diverse and inclusive company full of brilliant people with different skills, experiences and perspectives. All applicants will be considered without regard to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, veteran status, neurodiversity or disability.

If this sounds like your kind of thing, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t tick every box. We’d love to hear from you. 

Compensation: £50K – £70K

title: Senior Creative, Social
description:

Creating end-to-end solutions that bring audience expectations and platform algorithms together with relevance, clarity and cultural resonance.

Job Description

The Senior Creative, Social is a hands-on conceptual thinker and maker who can bridge the worlds of advertising and social. This isn't just a BAU role. You’ll be as comfortable cracking a big campaign platform, activation or experiential idea as you are creating culturally relevant, platform-native social work. We’re looking for someone who understands that the best social ideas aren’t simply content, they’re ideas people want to talk about, participate in and share.

Working closely with our Creative Directors and wider creative teams, you’ll develop ideas from first thought through to execution, helping us create work that moves seamlessly between campaigns, activations, content and culture. This is a role for someone ambitious about the work. Someone with a strong conceptual advertising brain, a deep understanding of social platforms and culture, and a portfolio that demonstrates both. We want to see evidence of award-winning ideas, not just beautifully executed content.

This is a hybrid position, based out of our London office. The salary range for this position is between £70,000-78,000 GBP, annually, and a final offer is dependent on experience.

Responsibilities

Conceptual & Social Creativity

  • Develop bold, original ideas across social, campaigns, activations, experiential, digital and emerging platforms.

  • Bring the same conceptual ambition to a TikTok, Reel or reactive social opportunity as you would to a major integrated campaign brief.

  • Think beyond posts and content calendars to create social ideas that can earn attention, conversation and cultural relevance.

  • Turn cultural observations, audience behaviours, platform trends and brand truths into simple, powerful creative ideas.

  • Understand the difference between following culture and contributing to it, and constantly look for opportunities for our brands to do the latter.

  • Create ideas that can start in social and grow into something bigger, as well as finding compelling social expressions of larger campaign platforms.

  • Bring an award-winning mentality to briefs of every size, continually pushing the work beyond the expected.

  • Work closely with Creative Directors to develop, challenge and elevate ideas from initial concept through to final execution.

Leadership & Creative Culture

  • Mentor and inspire junior creatives, designers and content creators, helping them strengthen both their conceptual thinking and social craft.

  • Give clear, constructive feedback that makes ideas stronger rather than simply different.

  • Help build a creative culture that is ambitious, collaborative, curious and relentlessly focused on the quality of the work.

Social & Cultural Fluency

  • Stay obsessively curious about internet culture, entertainment, technology, creators, memes, trends and emerging behaviours.

  • Understand platform conventions without becoming constrained by them.

  • Bring a strong point of view on what makes work genuinely social rather than simply advertising placed on social platforms.

  • Help educate clients and internal teams on evolving social behaviours, creative opportunities and emerging formats.

Creative Craft & Making

  • Take ideas from blank page through to execution, including concepts, scripts, social formats, treatments, storyboards, copy, creator briefs and presentations.

  • Use GenAI and emerging creative technologies as genuine creative tools to explore, prototype, make and push ideas further rather than simply make things faster.

  • Be comfortable making and prototyping ideas yourself when it helps bring thinking to life quickly.

  • Work closely with creators, designers, writers, editors, producers and production partners to maintain the integrity of an idea throughout production.

  • Understand how craft changes by platform, audience and context without compromising the strength of the underlying idea.

  • Continually experiment with new tools, formats and production approaches that could unlock new creative possibilities.

  • Bring innovation (particularly AI and emerging technologies) into both the thinking and making of our work.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years within advertising, social or creative agencies, with experience operating at Senior Creative level.

  • A conceptual creative first with a strong advertising brain and can reduce a complicated brief to a simple, powerful idea.

  • You are socially fluent and understand platforms, creators, communities, formats and internet culture deeply enough to create work that belongs there.

  • Experience moving comfortably between campaign platforms, activations and experiential ideas and fast-moving, culturally relevant social content.

  • Deep understanding of how people actually use TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Reddit and emerging social platforms, including the behaviours, communities, creators and formats that shape them.

  • You have created, or can demonstrate the potential to create, work capable of competing at the highest creative level.

  • Experience with the nuanced rules and behaviours of individual platforms but don't allow formats or trends to become substitutes for ideas.

  • Ability to articulate ideas simply, write compelling copy and scripts, and build persuasive creative presentations.

  • Strong presentation experience with the ability to sell an idea, defend the thinking behind it and bring clients and collaborators with you.

  • Experience using tools such as ChatGPT, Midjourney, Kling and other emerging creative technologies as part of your creative process.

Note: We emphasise skills, expertise and behavioural attributes over years of experience and traditional degrees. If you want to join our collaborative team, we invite you to apply today with your resume in English.

Additional Information

Join Jellyfish and experience a workplace where we prioritise your growth, celebrate your contributions, and empower you to tailor your work environment to suit your needs.

💰 Reward: You'll be eligible to join our discretionary annual bonus scheme.

💫 Custom Work Environment: Work remotely for up to 60% of your days and shape your day between 8am. and 6:30pm with flexible working hours.

title: Financial Auditor – Product & Methodology
description:
About Cortea

We're Cortea, a European audit-tech company, born in Berlin, rebuilding how audits are done everywhere.

Audits are still driven by spreadsheets, checklists, and manual reviews in one of the most regulated, high-stakes areas of business. We use AI to automate audits end to end, so highly educated auditors no longer spend 60+ hour weeks on manual work and can focus on judgment, trust, and choices that matter.

With €15m+ in funding, a live product, and paying customers across Europe, we're at a stage where your choices will directly shape Cortea's future, and how audits are done.

The Role

This is a role for an auditor with a deep interest in audit methodology: someone who knows the standards in detail, recognises where they leave room for interpretation, and wants to build the tools they always wished they had. Someone who is curious about the newest tools and tech trends entering the ecosystem, and has built a point of view on how the industry can best be served by tech, AI and innovation. Reporting to Philipp (Co-Founder), you sit closer to the product than a typical audit hire: you translate audit methodology into structured logic, write and refine the prompts that drive our AI workflows, and work day to day with our engineering team in Berlin to shape how audit logic is built, tested, and shipped. No programming background is required. What matters is rigorous process thinking and a deep understanding of how audits actually get done.

Key Responsibilities

  • Product Shaping: Work as a standing part of the product process: join reviews and design sessions, give hands-on feedback on prototypes, and help prioritise the roadmap

  • Methodology to Logic: Translate complex ISA (UK) and international auditing standards into structured, executable logic our product and engineering team can build directly into the platform

  • Prompt Engineering: Write, test, and refine the prompts and decision logic that drive our AI audit workflows

  • Documentation Quality: Ensure audit documentation quality aligns with ISA (UK) 230 and related documentation requirements, and that system outputs stand up to internal quality control and external review

  • Independence & Ethics: Safeguard auditor independence and ensure the product complies with the FRC Ethical Standard and ICAEW/ACCA Code of Ethics

  • Berlin Collaboration: Travel regularly to our Berlin hub to work in person with Philipp and the product and engineering team


Requirements

  • Minimum 5 years of financial audit experience (Big 4 or leading mid-tier firms preferred), including time at audit manager level with a solid understanding of engagement responsibility and audit risk

  • ACA (ICAEW), ACCA, or equivalent chartered accountancy qualification

  • A strong interest in audit methodology: you enjoy turning abstract standards into clear, reproducible logic

  • A tech-first mindset and a proven willingness to leverage, experiment with, or build new tools, with relentless curiosity for how AI and innovation can improve work and outcomes

  • Ability to sketch decision trees and define structured, unambiguous process outputs; comfortable writing and iterating on AI prompts

  • No programming background required, but you think in processes, dependencies, and system logic, and enjoy working closely with engineers day to day

  • Strong grasp of ISA (UK), UK GAAP (FRS 102), IFRS, and the Companies Act 2006

  • Native in English, German is a plus

Benefits

  • Competitive salary plus equity participation

  • The chance to build the tools you always wished you'd had as an auditor, with direct influence over product direction

  • Hybrid collaboration from our London office, with regular trips to our Berlin hub

  • 25+ days holiday allowance

  • Pension contribution

  • Private medical insurance

Interview Process

  • Intro call with Liza (Founders Associate)

  • Technical audit & methodology interview with Philipp (Co-Founder)

  • Strategic & Collaboration Fit interview with Valentin (Co-Founder)

  • On-site session (Berlin/London): work through a "reviewer-first" interface design exercise, focused on transparency, traceability, and professional scepticism

description:
Senior Data Protection Engineer (Backup & Cyber Resilience)

Location: Windsor, UK

Introduction

We’re hiring a Senior Data Protection Engineer to join a global hosting and managed services team. The team runs business-critical, highly regulated systems for organisations around the world, many of them in healthcare, where losing data or failing to recover it is not an option.

This is a senior role with real influence. You’ll own the enterprise backup and recovery platform across all regions. You’ll set the standards for how data is protected, retained and restored, and you’ll show, with evidence, that recovery targets are met. You’ll also help shape where data protection services go next, at a time when cyber resilience matters more than ever.

Responsibilities & Tasks

  • Run the platform globally. Lead the engineering, administration and continuous improvement of an enterprise Rubrik environment. This covers configuration, upgrades, capacity planning, health monitoring, security hardening and lifecycle management.

  • Set the rules. Design and enforce global protection policies, including SLA tiers, retention, archiving, replication, immutability, encryption and access controls.

  • Turn requirements into protection. Convert business, regulatory, contractual and risk needs into clear protection tiers, RPO and RTO targets, and practical operating procedures.

  • Keep coverage complete. Bring new workloads into the service and keep protection accurate across on-premises, cloud, virtualised, database and application environments.

  • Keep operations healthy. Monitor backup, replication, archiving and restore activity. Fix failed jobs, capacity pressure, performance issues and policy exceptions before they become risks.

  • Prove that recovery works. Plan and run restore tests, disaster recovery exercises and readiness reviews, and keep the evidence that recovery targets and controls are met.

  • Strengthen cyber resilience. Work with security and incident response teams on ransomware readiness, anomaly investigations, clean-recovery planning and privileged-access controls.

  • Build strong governance. Write the runbooks, standards and procedures that define good practice, and help regions and technology teams adopt them consistently.

  • Lead when it counts. Take technical ownership during incidents and service disruptions, and drive root cause analysis and lasting corrective actions.

  • Automate. Use APIs, scripting and orchestration tools to automate routine operations, compliance checks, reporting and workflows.

  • Report clearly. Give regular insight into protection coverage, recoverability, compliance, capacity, platform risk and operational performance.

  • Work across teams. Partner closely with infrastructure, cloud, database, application, security, risk and business continuity colleagues, and take part in a shared on-call rota for critical production services.

Requirements & Qualifications

Essential:

  • A solid track record of engineering and running enterprise-scale backup, recovery and data protection services

  • Extensive hands-on production experience with Rubrik

  • A current Rubrik Certified System Administrator (RCSA) certification

  • Experience designing and rolling out data protection policies, standards and operating models across multiple regions

  • A strong grasp of retention, immutability, encryption, access control, RPO and RTO, and recovery validation

  • Hands-on involvement in disaster recovery, cyber recovery or ransomware-resilience initiatives

  • Strong troubleshooting skills, and familiarity with incident, change and problem management processes

  • Experience supporting production services in a 24x7 or on-call environment

Benefits & Culture

  • Global reach and visible impact: Your work will directly protect critical services, including healthcare systems that clinicians and care providers rely on every day.

  • Real ownership: You’ll have a strong voice in policy design, retention strategy, cyber resilience, automation and the long-term direction of the service.

  • Collaborative environment: You’ll join experienced engineers and architects who value shared ownership, operational excellence and openly sharing knowledge.

  • Growth and development: You’ll keep developing your skills on an enterprise-grade platform, with support for certifications and continuous learning.

  • Competitive rewards: The package includes market-aligned pay and comprehensive benefits that reflect a senior technical role.

If you want to make data protection dependable at a global scale, we’d love to hear from you.

We’re hiring a Product Manager with deep UX and interaction design expertise to build social experiences around investing and trading at Kraken.


You should be comfortable designing flows yourself, building interactive prototypes, and working through interaction details with designers and engineers. You’ll also own the product decisions: which customer problem to solve, what to ship first, and how to measure whether the experience improved.

 

The opportunity

  • Design complete social journeys. Work through how someone discovers a person, decides to follow them, shares an idea or trade, receives a response, and returns. Connect these interactions into an experience users understand without explanation.

  • Make the interaction details work. Shape navigation, information hierarchy, copy, defaults, gestures, and feedback. Specify what happens when a feed is empty, a post fails, content loads slowly, or someone changes their mind.

  • Prototype before committing to a build. Turn ideas into interactive prototypes that communicate the intended behavior. Explore alternatives, test the uncertain parts, and give engineering clear flows, states, and acceptance criteria.

  • Use psychology to improve participation. Understand why people hesitate to post, seek recognition, follow strangers, or respond to others. Translate those motivations into decisions about audience visibility, prompts, reputation, feedback, and the effort required to contribute.

  • Observe users and fix what gets in their way. Run usability sessions, watch people complete tasks, and combine those observations with funnel data. Identify where people misunderstand the product, lose confidence, or abandon an action.

  • Design for first use and repeated use. Make the experience useful before someone has connections. Keep sharing lightweight during an active trading session, with clear control over what becomes public. Test the twentieth interaction as carefully as the first.

  • Connect design decisions to measurable outcomes. For each significant change, define the expected behavior and how to test it. Track task completion, abandonment, first follows, first contributions, responses, and subsequent retention. Work with data science to evaluate experiments and effects on both contributors and their audiences.

  • Take the experience through launch. Choose a focused initial scope, resolve trade-offs with engineering, review the implementation against the intended design, and use post-launch evidence to decide what to improve next.

 

What you bring

  • Has designed and shipped consumer social experiences. Your portfolio shows your contribution to feeds, profiles, sharing, messaging, discovery, or communities—and how the experience changed after launch.

  • Has strong interaction design craft. You can explain why a flow is structured a particular way, what users will notice first, what they need to understand, and which decisions or steps can be removed.

  • Can build realistic interactive prototypes. You use Figma, code, AI tools, or a combination to make behavior tangible and testable, including transitions, empty states, and failure states.

  • Understands behavior through evidence. You can show where user research challenged your assumptions and changed a design.

  • Can own product outcomes. You can prioritize a problem, define success, interpret funnel and cohort data, and explain whether an experiment produced a meaningful improvement.

  • Understands the context of social finance. You account for how credibility, incentives, reputation, and visibility of financial activity affect what people trust and choose to share.

title: Founding Product Builder, Operations
description:
Odin is building the investment infrastructure for the future of private markets.
We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should know how to put it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in.

Our first product is a full-stack platform for launching and running private investment firms, allowing you to run everything from your phone - think Shopify for VC and PE. We handle all the infrastructure: from legal structuring and investor onboarding to KYC/AML, payments, tax, reporting, and exits.

We're already trusted by over 10,000 angels, VCs, and founders. We administer over $750m in assets, covering investments from pre-seed to series E. This includes household names like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, SpaceX, xAI, Anduril, etc. but also new companies creating everything from synthetic brains to small nuclear reactors.

Why we're hiring

  • We are automating a decades old part of the financial services industry. AI pilled builders like you are the beating heart of this plan, because LLMs & agents allow us to turn this services business entirely into software.

  • This is a product role, and your product is how Odin operates. Think of it as our ghostbuster: every operational problem lands with you, you decide what gets fixed, and you ship most of the fixes yourself rather than writing tickets for someone else.

  • We're post-PMF, fast-growing, and rolling out new products (fund admin) & geographies (USA). Customer & deal volume is climbing fast.

  • Today we're on track for roughly 700 deals a year, with a team of ~20, and we'll process $500m-$750m of investment in 2026 alone.

  • The next goal is 7,000 deals a year and billions in annual investment flows.

  • We believe this can be achieved with a team of around 50 people. But it will only be possible if we turn human-driven services workflows into software.

  • Odin's operations run on around 50 processes, some code and some people, and plenty still held together by spreadsheets. Your job is to take each one apart, question why it exists, then rebuild it or kill it.

  • The simplest way to think about it: the numerator is how many deals we close, the denominator is what each deal costs us to run. You'll focus on the denominator, and the right person won't be able to stop themselves thinking about the numerator too.

  • We expect the right hire to be spending more time in Claude Code than in Excel, email or anything else.

What you'll own

  • Triage: Every operational problem comes to you before it reaches product and engineering. For each one you decide: scope it so precisely that engineering knows exactly what to build, or build it yourself.

  • Cost per deal: There will be big early wins where a whole process can be ripped out and replaced. After that, doubling ops efficiency comes from 150 small changes, and you'll be the one making them.

  • Automation: You'll sit with the deal operations team, learn each workflow end to end, then build what replaces it. Most of what you ship you'll build without engineering. What does go to them arrives simple, scoped and usually with a working prototype attached.

  • Deleting things and saying no: You decide what belongs in our processes and what doesn't. If a request from sales doesn't scale and isn't highly profitable we don't do it. If a way of working exists for no good reason, you kill it.

  • The ops team: You'll lead the core deal operations team, deciding where their time goes while you rebuild the work around them.

What we're looking for

  • You build, not buy: Clear evidence, at work or in your own time, that you've built real solutions with AI with no budget and no engineers. Buying a tool or setting up workflows in Sheets doesn't count. We want to see what you've shipped in Claude Code or similar.

  • Founder or product DNA: You've founded something, been early on a founding team, or worked as a product manager. That usually means four or more years of experience and a track record of finishing what you start.

  • Systems thinker: You look at any process the way a good product manager looks at a product: What's the job? Why are we doing this at all? What's the smallest, simplest system that achieves the goal? You think about the whole business, not just your corner of it.
    A lot of what happens in fund admin is inherited convention, an industry "given", or a constraint of some third party. You should find it physically difficult to accept any of that.

  • In the details and extremely on top of things: You understand every single aspect of our systems end to end. You close loops, you chase, you push hard to get things done.

  • Numerate: Comfortable with financial mechanics, strong mental arithmetic. You'll be automating a lot of numerical work - carry, allocations, fee calculations, distributions, and the edge cases that make all of them interesting.

  • Big plus: regulated financial services background: Fund administration, custody, payments, brokerage, audit, tax or another back office function. Useful, but not required. We care much more about the traits you have and the things you can build than specific skills or experience on your CV.

How we work

There are five things we care about deeply:

  1. Reason from the ground up
    Seek to understand what is true by always asking why. Do not trust convention or experts.

  2. Speed begets speed
    We work fast. Speed compounds, it's the best form of defensibility, and it's energising to be around. If you work slowly, or tolerate slow work around you, you do not belong at Odin.

  3. Take ownership
    Do not wait for permission to do things. Find the answer, force the thing into existence and hold others to an extremely high standard - the same standard you hold yourself to.

  4. Brutal honesty
    If work doesn't meet the bar, people need to hear it, and the right people want to.

  5. Truly excellent customer service
    Be a stickler for detail in every single interaction a customer has with us, and always strive to make this experience better, smoother, faster.

This role is probably not for you if

  • You'd rather write specs and hand tickets to engineers than build the thing yourself;

  • You prefer close management of your responsibilities;

  • You are risk-averse;

  • You want a 9-5;

  • You take yourself too seriously;

  • You care about working for a company that's raised lots of money rather than one that's extremely capital efficient and focused on building a profitable giant that has a positive economic impact

Salary

£90k - £120k base, plus a meaningful equity grant. We're flexible on the mix of cash and equity.

Hiring process

Three stages, usually inside two weeks, with detailed feedback within 24 hours of each one. A call with our Head of People, an in-person session with the founders where you solve a real Odin problem end to end with AI, then a final with the founders. The last two can run on the same day.

Location & ways of working

We're a London-based team. This role works closely with the founders, product and the wider ops team, and the speed we run at makes that much easier in-person. At least three days a week in the office.

Benefits

  • Health: Private health insurance (Vitality), paid sick leave including support for pregnancy loss and fertility treatments, and access to Spill for mental health support

  • Wellness: £1,000 annual budget for health, therapy or fitness

  • Parental Leave: Enhanced maternity, adoption, paternity and partner leave

  • Pension: 4% employer contribution with salary sacrifice options

  • Time Off: 25 days annual leave, 2 wellness days and flexible bank holidays (33 days total)

  • Work From Anywhere: Up to 6 weeks per year working from anywhere globally

  • Birthday Leave: An additional day of leave

title: Implementation Specialist

title: Software Engineer (Fleet) - London
description:
About Us

At Teton, we are redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology. Facing a global nursing shortage, our solutions offer vital support to overburdened health systems. The Job

Every patient room we deploy into puts another device on infrastructure we don't control, in a building we can't easily visit, running software that has to keep working. We're looking for an Engineer to own that problem: the systems, tooling, and infrastructure that let us ship to thousands of edge devices confidently and understand what they're doing once they're out there.

In this role, you will focus on the following areas of interest:

  • Fleet Management: Build and run the systems that provision, monitor, and manage our devices in the field, from first boot in a hospital room to end of life.

  • OTA & Release Engineering: Own how software gets onto devices: staged rollouts, health checks, automatic rollback, and the confidence that a bad release won't take down a ward.

  • Observability: Design the telemetry, logging, and alerting that tell us a device is degrading before a nurse notices. Make remote debugging possible so we don't fly to fix things.

  • Device Bring-Up & Debugging: Work with our hardware and firmware teams on new hardware revisions, reproduce field issues on the bench, and get to the bottom of problems that span kernel, driver, network, and application.

  • Infrastructure & Tooling: Build the CI/CD, image builds, and internal tools that let the whole engineering team ship to hardware quickly and safely.

  • Documentation: Maintain clear and detailed documentation of your work to ensure easy collaboration and knowledge sharing within the team.

Qualifications:

  • Solid experience running Linux systems in production: ideally embedded or edge Linux, not just cloud VMs.

  • Proficiency in Rust and/or Javascript/Typescript and/or Python

  • Experience with device fleets at scale: provisioning, OTA update mechanisms (Mender, RAUC, balena, or something you built yourself), and remote access to constrained devices.

  • Familiarity with Linux internals: systemd, kernel modules, device tree, networking stack, containers.

  • Experience with observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or similar) and designing what to measure, not just wiring up dashboards.

  • Comfortable with hardware debugging: serial consoles, working alongside hardware engineers

  • Understanding of communication protocols and how devices talk to each other and to us: I2C, SPI, UART, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, MQTT.

  • Pragmatism about networks you don't control: restrictive hospital IT, VLANs, proxies, flaky Wi-Fi, and long offline periods.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently as well as part of a team.

  • Experience with the NVIDIA Jetson platform and Linux for Tegra is a big plus.

  • Experience with Yocto, Debian packaging, or custom image builds is a plus.

  • Experience in the medical device or healthcare technology field is a plus.

What We Offer

Everyone has the potential to build something great for the world. But fulfilling that ambition almost always requires more: people willing to trust you with their capital. Yet access to capital still depends on where you live, who you know, and which institutions are willing to trust you. Even when capital is available, it sits fragmented across disconnected networks and hidden behind intermediaries. The result is a system that fails most of the people it should serve. Borrowers overpay. Lenders earn less than they should. Many are shut out entirely, not because they are unworthy of credit, but because today's infrastructure was never built to connect them. Morpho exists to solve this. Full article here.
